The individuals profiled come from prominent firms like Goldman Sachs, Blackstone, and Apollo, showcasing diverse roles and remarkable achievements, such as running hedge funds, leading major investments, and pioneering new financial strategies. The selection highlights their innovative approaches and rapid career progression in the competitive finance industry.

title: Big bank earnings are about to kick off—here are 3 ways to play the deluge
summary: As big bank earnings season kicks off, experts suggest investing in larger banks through ETFs like the Financial Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLF) due to their diversified revenue streams and deeper capital market structures in a low-rate environment. Investors are advised to look closely at the holdings within regional banking ETFs like iShares Regional Bank ETF (IAT) and SPDR S&P Regional Banking ETF (KRE) to understand their exposure to larger regional players versus smaller, more loan-dependent institutions. The article emphasizes doing thorough research on ETF portfolios beyond just volume.

title: The Big Interview: Goldman Sachs AM’s EMEA ETF head Thompson reveals plans for European business
summary: Peter Thompson, head of ETFs, EMEA, at Goldman Sachs Asset Management (GSAM), unveiled plans for a significant expansion in the European ETF market, including the launch of up to 10 new ETFs by Q1. GSAM will focus on smart beta strategies, particularly in fixed income, and target retail and intermediary segments in fragmented European markets like Germany, Switzerland, and the UK. Thompson stressed the importance of leveraging existing Goldman Sachs relationships and expanding capital markets expertise despite entering the market later than some competitors.

title: MGM to sell Bellagio, Circus Circus resorts for about $5 billion
summary: MGM Resorts International announced the sale of its Bellagio and Circus Circus resorts in Las Vegas for approximately $5 billion. The Bellagio will be acquired by Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust in a joint venture and leased back to MGM, while Circus Circus will be sold to an affiliate of Treasure Island owner Phil Ruffin. MGM aims to use the proceeds to strengthen its balance sheet and return capital to shareholders as part of a move to an asset-light model.

title: The commercial real estate media source.
summary: Annemarie DiCola, CEO of Trepp, hosted a CREW New York coffee meeting focusing on finance, investment, and capital markets in commercial real estate. The event was attended by numerous women in real estate from major financial institutions, including Societe General, Credit Agricole, Bank ABC, and Arbor Realty Trust. Attendees discussed finance, investment, and capital markets within CRE.

title: PNC to move into new local HQ as it expands in Boston
summary: PNC Bank is planning to move into a new local headquarters in Boston as part of its expansion efforts in the city. The regional president of the Pittsburgh-based banking giant discussed PNC's local hiring and philanthropic plans, as well as its strategy for retail branches in the area. This move follows previous announcements regarding PNC's decision to open its first retail branches in Boston and establish a regional president for its expansion.

title: BlackRock’s $7trn AUM dominated by index and ETF products
summary: BlackRock's assets under management (AUM) reached $6.96 trillion by the end of September 2019, primarily driven by its index and ETF businesses which collectively accounted for 65% of total assets. The firm saw significant net inflows of $84.2 billion in Q3, with indexation and iShares ETFs contributing substantially, especially in fixed income products which outpaced equity ETFs during the quarter and year-to-date. Larry Fink highlighted the strength in fixed income, cash, and alternative strategies as clients re-balanced amidst market volatility.

title: Bank of America may be as profitable as J.P. Morgan in two years, analyst says
summary: Edward Jones analyst James Shanahan suggests that Bank of America could achieve profitability similar to J.P. Morgan within two years, making it a better investment over the next few years. He attributes this potential to Bank of America's record $7.6 billion in share buybacks in Q3 and significant investments in technology, which are expected to boost earnings performance and market share. Share buybacks contribute to higher earnings per share and improved returns on equity.

title: Why JPMorgan Chase Wants to Give More Former Criminals a Second Chance
summary: JPMorgan Chase is taking significant steps to promote second-chance hiring for individuals with criminal records, including removing criminal record questions from job applications and directing over $7 million to organizations that train formerly incarcerated individuals. The bank is also establishing a new "policy center" to advocate for regulatory changes that currently bar former felons from employment, with an initial focus on easing rules for financial institutions. CEO Jamie Dimon views this as part of a broader economic revitalization campaign, inspired by the challenges faced by "returning citizens."

title: Real estate and Wall Street bolster embattled Staten Island congressman
summary: Staten Island Rep. Max Rose has received significant campaign contributions from real estate and Wall Street figures for his re-election bid. The Kimco Realty family made substantial donations, as did executives from Oaktree Capital, Lazard, and Dune Real Estate. These contributions are helping Rose in what is expected to be a contentious race against GOP Assemblywoman Nicole Malliotakis.

title: Post Holdings and BellRing Brands Announce Closing of
summary: Post Holdings and BellRing Brands announced the closing of BellRing's initial public offering of 39,428,571 shares of Class A common stock at $14.00 per share, including the full exercise of underwriters' option for additional shares. Following the offering, Post Holdings retains approximately 71% ownership of BellRing. BellRing's Class A common stock commenced trading on the NYSE under the symbol "BRBR" on October 17, 2019.

title: JPMorgan Chase Joins Second Chance Efforts to Reduce Obstacles to Employment
summary: JPMorgan Chase is expanding its commitment to supporting individuals with criminal backgrounds by focusing on public policy changes, investing over $7 million in community organizations, and enhancing its hiring strategies. The firm aims to reduce obstacles to employment for these individuals, thereby lowering recidivism rates and strengthening communities. This initiative includes launching a new PolicyCenter to advocate for policy solutions that drive inclusive economic growth, beginning with fair chance hiring.

title: Reynolds Wrap Maker Targets $7 Billion IPO Valuation
summary: Reynolds Consumer Products Inc., known for Reynolds Wrap and Hefty trash bags, is reportedly aiming for a $7 billion valuation in its upcoming U.S. initial public offering. The company has enlisted Credit Suisse Group AG, JPMorgan Chase & Co., and Goldman Sachs Group Inc. to manage the share sale, which could take place by the end of 2019 or in the first quarter of 2020.

title: Citigroup Puts a Woman in Line to Be Its C.E.O. (Published 2019)
summary: Citigroup appointed Jane Fraser as its president and chief executive of its global consumer banking business, positioning her to potentially become the bank's future CEO. This move makes Citigroup the first major U.S. bank to clearly indicate a woman for its top leadership role. The elevation of Ms. Fraser highlights the ongoing efforts to break the glass ceiling for women in top positions at the country's largest financial institutions.

title: As JPMorgan Chase expands in Minnesota, exec says there's no rush to get big
summary: JPMorgan Chase is taking a long-term, measured approach to its expansion in Minnesota, focusing on sustainable growth rather than rapid market share acquisition. Despite the market dominance of local banks, the company believes its retail presence and technological investments will help it build a strong commercial banking business. A top executive stated the bank views its presence in Minnesota with a 100-year horizon, prioritizing client value and optimized financial profiles over short-term gains.

title: AmEx ‘Green Card’ turns 50, gets a needed revamp
summary: The American Express Green Card, celebrating its 50th anniversary, is undergoing a significant revamp to modernize its offerings and appeal to contemporary travelers. The changes include a new look, enhanced travel benefits, a higher annual fee, and a shift from a traditional charge card to function more like a credit card with the option to revolve a balance. This strategic move aims to revive the card's popularity, which has declined over time in favor of its Gold and Platinum siblings, and adapt to evolving customer preferences in the credit card market.

title: Woman Says Scammers Drained Her Account Through Zelle, But Fifth Third Bank Told Her They 'Can't Prove Anything'
summary: A Vernon Hills woman, Deborah Steidl, reported that scammers drained $2,540 from her Fifth Third Bank account using Zelle. Despite her claims, Fifth Third Bank initially denied her fraud claims, stating "we have determined the transaction is valid," leaving her without recourse until a later update confirmed the money was refunded. The incident highlights potential vulnerabilities with Zelle and public computer use, though the exact method of the scam remains a mystery.

title: JPMorgan Chase shrinks workforce in NYC and Plano could benefit
summary: JPMorgan Chase is shrinking its workforce in New York City and is considering moving thousands of New York-based employees to lower-cost hubs like Plano, Texas, to rein in costs. The financial giant is building a new 12-story tower in Plano to house an additional 4,000 workers, potentially increasing its Plano workforce to almost 11,000. This move is influenced by high taxes and expensive real estate in New York, and aligns with a broader trend of financial institutions relocating employees to cheaper U.S. cities.

title: Wilmington could benefit if JPMorgan shifts jobs out of NYC
summary: Wilmington, Delaware, stands to gain if JPMorgan Chase & Co. relocates jobs from its New York City headquarters to more cost-effective markets. The bank is reviewing its employee and facility locations, although it remains committed to the New York area. This move could bring economic benefits to Wilmington as JPMorgan seeks to optimize its operational costs.

title: JPMorgan Chase considering shifting jobs out of New York, report says, with Columbus in the mix
summary: JPMorgan Chase is reportedly considering shifting jobs out of its expensive New York headquarters to regional hubs like Columbus, Ohio, to manage rising costs. Columbus has been a significant growth area for the bank, which continues to evaluate the best locations for its workforce. This move could further bolster the bank's presence in existing regional operational centers.

title: Sallie Mae expands into cards amid dearth of competition for student credit
summary: Sallie Mae has launched three cash-back credit cards targeting students and recent graduates, capitalizing on reduced competition in the student credit market after the 2009 CARD Act. This move aims to promote financial responsibility but raises concerns about potentially increasing debt for students already struggling with loans. The company emphasizes its commitment to responsible lending and has implemented measures to address loan defaults, despite critics' worries about the expansion.

title: JPMorgan CEO says lessons learned from failed WeWork IPO
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co CEO Jamie Dimon defended the bank's advisory role in WeWork's failed IPO but acknowledged that valuable lessons were learned from the experience. Dimon emphasized the importance of proper corporate governance for companies going public. JPMorgan Chase, with Dimon as chairman, was the lead investment bank advising WeWork.

title: JPMorgan Chase targets gig economy tech firms with e-wallet platform
summary: JPMorgan Chase has developed an e-wallet platform aimed at gig economy companies like Airbnb, Lyft, and Amazon, offering virtual bank accounts and perks to customers. This strategy allows JPMorgan to assume payment processing for these tech firms, addressing the threat of revenue loss to nonbanks and fintech companies. The bank aims to partner with the top 10 e-commerce and gig economy companies, simplifying refund processes and expediting payouts.

title: Wells Fargo CEO Scharf taps Daley to help fix bank's image
summary: Wells Fargo CEO Charlie Scharf has appointed Bill Daley, former White House chief of staff, as vice chairman of public affairs to improve relations with Washington. This move aims to rebuild trust with regulators and lawmakers following years of scandals and 14 outstanding consent orders. Daley's extensive experience in banking and politics is expected to help the bank address its image problems and accelerate reforms.

title: Improving Mortgage Customer Experience With Digitalization
summary: The mortgage industry has historically neglected customer experience, leading to frustration and disengagement among borrowers. This article highlights how digitalization and fintechs are transforming the mortgage process by streamlining applications, reducing costs, and improving customer satisfaction, forcing traditional banks to adapt or lose market share. It details several grassroots customer issues and how technology-driven solutions are addressing them.

title: BMO Harris plans downtown Sarasota move next year
summary: BMO Harris Bank is relocating its main Sarasota office to The Mark, a new mixed-use building at 1400 State St., by November 2020. This move signifies an upgrade to a more modern and visible downtown location for the bank, which reported $266.5 million in deposits. The article also touches on Bank of America's wage increases and a recent, unusual cluster of three U.S. bank failures.

title: Microsoft tops list of the most ‘just’ US corporations
summary: Microsoft Corp. has topped the list of America's Most JUST Companies for the second consecutive year, recognized for its commitment to workers, communities, and the environment. The nonprofit JUST Capital's rankings highlight corporations that prioritize all stakeholders, not just shareholders, addressing concerns about wealth inequality and climate change. The study analyzed 922 companies on issues like fair wages, environmental protection, and ethical business practices, with tech companies like NVIDIA and Apple also ranking high.

title: Everything So Far Has Failed: Why Exxon Mobil Is Being Taken to Court Over Climate Change
summary: Exxon Mobil is facing a wave of climate change litigation, with a New York trial being the first of its kind to target a fossil fuel company directly. The case, People of the State of New York v. Exxon Mobil Corp., focused on alleged securities fraud regarding Exxon's representations to shareholders about climate risks. This litigation, alongside similar cases in Massachusetts and other states, aims to hold the fossil fuel industry accountable for contributing to the climate emergency and for misleading the public about scientific consensus.

title: European banks are ‘too small to survive’: UBS CEO
summary: UBS Group AG CEO Sergio Ermotti states that European banks are too small to compete with their U.S. counterparts and require consolidation for survival and growth. He argues that too many banks in Europe cannot cover their cost of capital, making "critical mass" essential in the banking sector to remain globally competitive. Ermotti also suggests cooperation with domestic players in target markets to avoid high costs associated with gaining market share.

title: Spain Overtakes U.K. as Europe’s Worst Stock Market After Vote
summary: Following a recent election and the prospect of a coalition with an anti-austerity party, the IBEX benchmark has dropped 2.5% this week, making Spain's stock market the worst-performing in Europe. Banks are leading the losses, contributing to a fourth consecutive day of decline for the broader index. This downturn comes despite an earlier rally that had Spanish stocks nearing their year's highs.

title: CRH reportedly looks to sell Philippine operations
summary: CRH is reportedly considering selling its Philippine cement business, Republic Cement, to raise cash by divesting non-core assets. JP Morgan Chase is assisting with finding a buyer, and the operations could be valued between US$2-3 billion, with interest from Asian and European bidders. CRH acquired Republic Cement in 2015, which is the second-largest cement producer in the Philippines with 7.5Mta capacity from five plants.

title: Gold, Silver Move Higher as Risk-Off Sentiment Reigns
summary: Precious metals, gold and silver, saw price increases due to a rise in risk-averse sentiment among traders and investors, making them attractive safe-haven assets. This upward movement was further fueled by short-term futures traders buying back positions and was influenced by ongoing impeachment hearings, Federal Reserve testimony, and renewed uncertainties in U.S.-China trade relations. Technical analysis indicates that while bears still hold a slight near-term advantage, buyers are looking to shift the market dynamic for both gold and silver.

title: JPMorgan Chase Partners With Paul Quinn College on its Urban Work College Program
summary: JPMorgan Chase is partnering with Paul Quinn College's Urban Work College program, making it the program's largest Plano employer. This collaboration allows 22 students to work at the bank while completing their studies, gaining experience in business, finance, and technology. The initiative supports JPMorgan Chase's Advancing Black Pathways program to hire 4,000 Black students over five years, aiming to provide education, careers, and wealth opportunities.

title: Investing for Income with Durable Dividends
summary: This article discusses the ongoing search for yield among investors, particularly with low interest rates and increasing negative-yielding government debt. It highlights the potential pitfalls of traditional dividend strategies, such as "dividend traps," and introduces a "Durable Dividends Strategy" that focuses on attractively priced companies with strong financial health and the ability to sustain dividend payments, as exemplified by the VanEck Vectors Morningstar Durable Dividend ETF (DURA).

title: Pros, Cons to Buying JPMorgan Chase & Co. (JPM) Stock
summary: This article weighs the pros and cons of investing in JPMorgan Chase & Co. (JPM) stock as of late 2019. Despite a challenging interest rate environment, JPMorgan posted record earnings due to a strong U.S. consumer and boosted its dividend and stock buyback program, favored by analysts for its strong management and financials. However, concerns include the difficulty for outsiders to evaluate bank loan assets, dependence on higher interest rates, and a potentially peaking financial sector, suggesting it might not be the optimal time to buy despite JPM being a well-run bank.

title: JPMorgan Chase Invests $1M in North Texas Military Vets
summary: JPMorgan Chase is investing over $1 million to support military veterans in North Texas through partnerships with local organizations NPower, Bunker Labs, and Headstrong. These funds will facilitate veterans' transition to civilian life by providing IT industry training, encouraging entrepreneurship, and offering free mental health services. This initiative aims to make JPMorgan Chase an employer of choice for veterans and a bank of choice for veteran-owned businesses.

title: Feds sign off on $66 billion BB&T-SunTrust merger
summary: Federal regulators have approved the $66 billion merger between BB&T and SunTrust, paving the way for the creation of Truist Financial Corp. The merger is set to close on December 6, 2019, and will establish Truist as the sixth-largest bank in the nation.

title: A brief overview of U.S. Bank
summary: This article provides an overview of U.S. Bank, highlighting its position as the fifth-largest retail bank in the US by deposits and assets, holding $391 billion in assets as of September 2014. It discusses U.S. Bank's services, its size relative to the "big four" banks, and its strategic focus on a limited geographic area across 25 states in the West and Midwest. The bank operates through a network of 3,177 branches and 5,026 ATMs, including many located within grocery stores.

title: Why Bank of America’s commercial loan portfolio is diversified
summary: Bank of America's commercial loan portfolio is significantly diversified across industries, geographies, and customers to mitigate risk. At the end of 2013, commercial loans comprised over 40% of its total loan portfolio, with major concentrations in diversified financials and real estate. The bank's non-US portfolio is spread across various regions, with Europe accounting for the largest share.

title: Adding Sustainability to Bond Portfolios
summary: As ESG equity ETFs gained popularity, advisors and investors sought similar sustainability options for fixed income portfolios. ETF issuers responded by increasing ESG bond funds, including the iShares ESG U.S. Aggregate Bond ETF (EAGG) and the iShares ESG USD Corporate Bond ETF (SUSC). These funds aim to track indices composed of investment-grade bonds from issuers with favorable ESG practices, offering similar risk/return properties to traditional benchmarks with added portfolio resilience.

title: Collibra inducted into JPMorgan Chase Hall of Innovation
summary: Collibra, a Data Intelligence company, has been inducted into the JPMorgan Chase Hall of Innovation for its impactful contributions. This recognition highlights Collibra's innovative data strategy, business value, and disruptive nature in helping JPMorgan Chase manage metadata and enhance data governance. The company was honored at the 11th Annual J.P. Morgan Technology Innovation Symposium.

title: Nomura Securities Venture Wins First License to Do Business in China
summary: Nomura Holdings Inc.'s majority-owned securities joint venture in China has received the first securities business license issued to a foreign-controlled securities joint venture on the Chinese mainland. This development allows Nomura Orient International Securities to operate brokerage, investment consulting, proprietary trading, and asset management businesses, marking a significant step in China's financial market opening. The move aligns with China's broader initiative to grant foreign investors wider access to its financial sectors.

title: Charles Schwab TD Ameritrade merger: Charles Schwab to buy TD Ameritrade for $26 billion
summary: Charles Schwab is acquiring rival TD Ameritrade for $26 billion in a significant deal propelled by intense competition in the online brokerage industry. This merger combines the two largest players, creating a company with over $5 trillion in client assets, though it is expected to face antitrust scrutiny. The acquisition follows a trend of dropping fees in the investment industry, accelerating consolidation among financial services firms.

title: Charles Schwab agrees to buy TD Ameritrade for $26 billion
summary: Charles Schwab has agreed to acquire TD Ameritrade for $26 billion, creating a brokerage giant with 24 million customer accounts and over $5 trillion in client assets. This merger follows both companies' decisions to eliminate online trading commissions, a move that sparked a price war in the industry and raised questions about revenue replacement. The deal is expected to generate up to $2 billion in savings, although it may face antitrust scrutiny and concerns about reduced consumer choice.

title: Charles Schwab’s purchase of TD Ameritrade would create asset management giant
summary: Charles Schwab is acquiring TD Ameritrade in a $26 billion stock swap, a move spurred by widespread disruption and the elimination of online trading commissions in the brokerage industry. This merger would create a financial giant with over $5 trillion in client assets, positioning Schwab to save billions and offset lost revenue, though it may face antitrust scrutiny. The deal is indicative of potential broader consolidation within the industry as companies adapt to lower fees and increased competition.

title: Ex-Barclays executive: Qatar wanted to be bank’s ‘special’ Gulf
summary: During a fraud trial, a former Barclays executive, Roger Jenkins, testified that Qatar sought to be the bank's "special" Gulf partner in 2008 as Barclays needed to raise capital. Prosecutors allege that Barclays bankers improperly disguised £322 million in payments to Qatar as advisory services, misleading the market about the true nature of their fundraising during the financial crisis. Jenkins is one of several former executives facing charges related to these undisclosed payments, while Qatar and its former prime minister are not accused of wrongdoing.

title: Rentokil Initial is ranked the best place to work in Britain in a survey by Indeed
summary: Pest control and hygiene firm Rentokil Initial has been ranked the best company to work for in the UK by Indeed, unseating last year's winner Apple. The company was praised for its job security, advancement opportunities, work-life balance, and positive culture, based on reviews from its employees. The survey highlighted that companies need to offer more than just attractive salaries to secure top talent in today's job market.

title: JPMorgan Chase giving 2nd chance to those with criminal background
summary: JPMorgan Chase is implementing an initiative to hire individuals with criminal backgrounds, having already hired 2,100 such individuals in 2018. This effort is part of a broader trend where companies and governments are reconsidering hiring practices for ex-offenders, acknowledging that many have skills and deserve a second chance, especially given the low unemployment rate. The bank is also working with communities and leaders to address barriers to employment and develop skills for this demographic.

title: Citigroup globally established in emerging markets
summary: Citigroup has a strong global presence, with over 55% of its revenues derived from outside the US, significantly differentiating it from competitors like Bank of America and JPMorgan. The bank concentrates on emerging markets, which constitute about 43% of its revenues, offering substantial growth potential while managing risks through diversified operations and targeting investment-grade multinationals and high-credit quality consumers. This global strategy provides Citigroup with an early-mover advantage and the ability to expand operations across various markets.

title: Rentokil Initial tops league table of UK's most popular employers
summary: Rentokil Initial has been named the best company to work for in the UK, according to data from Indeed, surpassing 2018 winner Apple. The pest control and hygiene firm was praised for job security, advancement opportunities, work-life balance, and positive culture. British firms, including several high street brands and financial institutions, dominate the top 25 list of private sector employers, with employees valuing good work-life balance and positive work culture.

title: Tricia Griffith C-Suite 2019
summary: Tricia Griffith, President and CEO of Progressive Corp., was recognized in 2019 for her leadership, including a No. 61 ranking on Glassdoor's 100 best CEOs in America list. Under her leadership, Progressive saw 50% revenue growth over three years to $30 billion in 2018 and held the top spot in Crain's Cleveland Business' largest public companies list with a market cap over $45 billion as of April 2019. The company was also noted for its workplace diversity, scoring 85 points in a Wall Street Journal ranking of S&P 500 companies.

title: Banker of the Year: Citizens Bank's Bruce Van Saun
summary: This article highlights Bruce Van Saun's transformation of Citizens Financial Group from a struggling regional bank into an industry standout, leading to him being named American Banker’s Banker of the Year for 2019. Under his leadership, Citizens underwent a successful IPO and strategic repositioning, focusing on commercial and consumer lending, technological innovation, and improving company culture. The article details the bank's significant financial rebound, market share gains, and future challenges, such as cutting expenses and deepening customer relationships.

title: XP Inc. Announces Launch of Initial Public Offering
summary: XP Inc. announced the launch of its initial public offering of 72,510,641 Class A common shares, with an estimated price range of US$22.00 to US$25.00 per share. The company will list its shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol "XP" and detailed the global coordinators and joint bookrunners for the offering. This move aims to strengthen its capital structure and further its mission of democratizing access to financial products in Brazil.

title: GECAS and Sculptor Capital Management Close STARR 2019-2
summary: GECAS and Sculptor Capital Management announced the closing of STARR 2019-2, a transaction involving the sale of twenty Boeing and Airbus narrowbody aircraft with a total appraised value of approximately $539 million. Sculptor Capital will act as an asset manager on behalf of syndicated equity investors and has invested equity in START III Ltd., the entity acquiring the aircraft. This initiative aims to broaden the investor base in commercial aviation by bringing increased institutional capital.

title: FDIC report: Fifth Third Bank remains leader in Dayton's market share
summary: Fifth Third Bank has maintained its leading position in Dayton's local deposit market, according to a recent FDIC report. The bank saw an increase in both local deposits and market share. This content is featured in partnership with the Dayton Business Journal's banks list.

title: BB&T-SunTrust Merge to Form 6th Biggest Bank Truist Financial
summary: BB&T Corp and SunTrust Banks have merged to form Truist Financial Corp, creating the sixth largest commercial bank in the United States with over $450 billion in assets. The all-stock deal, approved by federal regulators, is expected to be earnings accretive for both companies' shareholders and result in $1.6 billion in pre-tax cost savings. The new entity, Truist Financial, will begin trading on the NYSE under the ticker "TFC" and is expected to provide significant competition to other major banks.

title: BB&T, SunTrust finish merger to become Truist in ‘seamless’ change. Here’s what’s next
summary: BB&T and SunTrust have finalized their $66 billion merger, officially becoming Truist Financial Corporation, the sixth-largest bank in the U.S. The integration process is expected to take 18-24 months, with branding rollout early next year, and the new headquarters will be in Charlotte's Hearst Tower, bringing 2,000 employees. The merger faced regulatory scrutiny and a trademark lawsuit, but the bank has also committed $60 billion to community investments.

title: SunTrust bank merger completed with BB&T, creating Truist
summary: The merger between SunTrust and BB&T has been finalized, creating Truist, the sixth-largest bank in the U.S. The new bank, headquartered in Charlotte, will serve approximately 10 million consumer households, with Atlanta retaining the corporate and investment banking division. The transition to the Truist brand is expected to take about two years, and the merged entity has committed significant financial support to communities in Winston-Salem and Atlanta.

title: Morgan Stanley is cutting jobs due to uncertain global environment, sources say
summary: Morgan Stanley is reportedly cutting approximately 2% of its global workforce, particularly in technology and operations roles, due to an uncertain global economic outlook. This move comes despite the bank exceeding analysts' expectations for third-quarter profit and revenue. The job cuts are seen as a proactive measure by Wall Street firms to manage costs at the end of the year, with Morgan Stanley being an early instance.

title: Morgan Stanley is cutting about 1,500 jobs
summary: Morgan Stanley is cutting approximately 1,500 jobs, representing over 2% of its workforce, primarily in technology and operations roles. These layoffs are a response to global economic uncertainty and pressure on Wall Street firms to control spending amidst low interest rates and slow economic growth. The bank expects to incur a charge of $150 million to $200 million due to the job cuts.

title: The 10 States Most Likely to Legalize Marijuana in 2020
summary: This article identifies the 10 states most likely to legalize marijuana in 2020, both recreationally and medically, based on current legislative efforts, public support, and signature-gathering for ballot initiatives. It highlights the significant financial opportunities for investors in the cannabis market as more states move towards legalization, potentially leading to a "gold rush" in the industry. The piece also discusses a surprising potential catalyst for legalization in Virginia and the impact of Illinois' recent legalization.

title: XP Inc. Announces Pricing of Initial Public Offering
summary: XP Inc. announced the pricing of its initial public offering of 72,510,641 Class A common shares at $27.00 per share. Trading is expected to begin on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on December 11, 2019, under the symbol "XP." The offering is set to close on December 13, 2019, with Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, J.P. Morgan, Morgan Stanley, XP Investments, and Itaú BBA acting as Global Coordinators.

title: J.P. Morgan Reorganizes U.S. Wealth Unit
summary: J.P. Morgan is reorganizing its U.S. Wealth Unit by combining J.P. Morgan Securities' approximately 450 brokers with 4,000 advisors in bank branches and the YouInvest online brokerage business under a new U.S. Wealth Management unit. This new unit will be led by Kristin Lemkau and aims to increase J.P. Morgan's share of the global wealth market, particularly focusing on its core banking clients. The reorganization is not expected to significantly affect compensation policies or product platforms but may allow for a slight increase in broker count.

title: Federal Reserve Lifts Consent Orders Against JPMorgan, U.S. Bancorp
summary: The Federal Reserve has lifted consent orders against JPMorgan Chase & Co. and U.S. Bancorp, which were initially issued due to identified weaknesses in their anti-money laundering controls. The order against JPMorgan, from January 2013, specifically required the bank to improve board oversight and management of compliance risks related to anti-money laundering. This action indicates that the central bank is satisfied with the improvements made by both financial institutions.

title: In Move To New Role At JPMorgan Chase, Kristin Lemkau Builds On Growth Priority As CMO
summary: Kristin Lemkau, previously CMO of JPMorgan Chase, has been named CEO of the bank’s wealth division, combining several wealth management segments to accelerate growth. Lemkau, recognized for her focus on growth and brand building, emphasized that the CMO role extends beyond traditional marketing to business development. Her move comes amidst a report of racial discrimination within JPMorgan Chase's banking business, though her response to how she'll address these issues was not immediately available.

title: Truist to buy uptown HQ building for $455.5M
summary: Charlotte-based Truist Financial Corp. is acquiring Hearst Tower in uptown from Cousins Properties for $455.5 million, rebranding it as Truist Center. This transaction, expected to close in March, will set a record for the highest sale price for a single office transaction in North Carolina. The building will house up to 2,000 Truist employees as the company relocates staff and hires new ones following the merger of BB&T and SunTrust Banks.

title: Park Place Dealerships sold to Georgia-based retailer in $1B transaction
summary: Park Place Dealerships has agreed to an all-cash $1 billion sale of 14 of its luxury car dealerships to Georgia-based Asbury Automotive Group Inc. The transaction, which excludes vehicle inventory, will see Asbury acquire 17 new vehicle franchises, primarily in the DFW metroplex, while founder Ken Schnitzer will retain two dealerships and a body shop in Grapevine. The deal is expected to close in Q1 2020 and significantly expands Asbury's presence in Texas.

title: JPMorgan Chase C.E.O. Says It Needs to Do More to Tackle Racism (Published 2019)
summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon addressed allegations of racism within the company in a memo to employees, stating that while progress on diversity and inclusion has been made, it's not enough. His comments followed a New York Times report detailing racist incidents at Phoenix-area branches and previous class-action lawsuits against the company regarding discrimination. Dimon emphasized the need for relentless effort and a review of policies to combat racism within the company.

title: XP Inc. Announces Closing of Initial Public Offering and
summary: XP Inc. announced the closing of its initial public offering of 83,387,237 Class A common shares at $27.00 per share, with shares trading on Nasdaq under "XP" since December 11, 2019. The offering included the full exercise of the underwriters' option to purchase additional shares from selling shareholders. XP received approximately US$1,100 million in net proceeds from its portion of the offering.

title: J.P. Morgan Reorganizes ETF Sales, Replaces U.S. Distribution Head
summary: J.P. Morgan Asset Management has reorganized its ETF sales division, merging its ETF specialists with broader asset management sales teams. This restructuring includes replacing U.S. ETF distribution head Jillian DelSignore with Bryon Lake, who will now oversee ETF sales in the U.S., Latin America, and Canada. The changes are part of a broader strategy to align ETF sales with the bank's asset management organization and follow another recent wealth management restructuring.

title: Top Hotels Sued for ‘Industry-Wide Failures’ to Prevent U.S. Sex Trafficking
summary: A landmark U.S. legal action has been filed against several major hotel groups, accusing them of profiting from sex trafficking due to "industry-wide failures" to prevent it on their premises. The lawsuit, on behalf of 13 women, consolidates existing cases and names twelve hotel chains, including Hilton, Red Roof Inn, and Wyndham, alleging they knew about and ignored warning signs of sex trafficking. This case marks the first time the hotel industry faces collective action for allegedly serving as a breeding ground for exploitation, with plaintiffs seeking unspecified damages and highlighting the prevalence of sex trafficking despite recent company initiatives.

title: The Green Assets Wallet – first blockchain for green bond impact data
summary: The Green Assets Wallet, a new blockchain database, has launched to provide a transparent platform for green bond data, aiming to unlock more credible investment opportunities with environmental impact. Developed over two years, it seeks to address the lack of reliable impact reporting in the green bonds market by offering an independent platform for issuers to showcase opportunities and report on deliverables, while investors gain access to trusted impact data. This initiative leverages blockchain technology to inject efficiency and trust into green bond impact reporting, potentially scaling up the market, especially in emerging economies.

title: New post for Buzzelli
summary: Robert Buzzelli has taken on new roles as managing director at TerraNova Capital Partners and shareholder in its parent company, New World Financial Holdings LLC. Buzzelli is a veteran of major financial institutions including U.S. Steel, BNY Mellon, and PNC.

title: An ETN Strategy Designed to Capitalized on a Steepening Yield Curve
summary: This article discusses an ETN strategy designed to capitalize on a steepening yield curve, focusing on the iPath US Treasury Steepener ETN (STPP). The ETN benefits from widening spreads between short-term and long-term Treasury yields, a trend recently observed as the U.S. Treasury yield curve hit its steepest point in over a year. The piece explains how STPP tracks a notional investment in Treasury futures contracts and examines the factors contributing to the current steepening, including Federal Reserve policy easing and improving economic figures.

title: Hombre más rico de Colombia suma US$3.000 millones a su fortuna
summary: Luis Carlos Sarmiento Angulo, Colombia's richest man, has seen his fortune increase by approximately US$3 billion due to the strong performance of his companies on the Colombian stock exchange. His financial conglomerate's firms, including Corficolombiana and Banco de Bogotá, led the Colcap index's gains in 2019, benefiting from robust consumer demand. This marks a significant turnaround from the previous year when the companies faced investor scrutiny over an investigation.

title: How I Used Miles and Points to Fly My Parents to Scotland
summary: The author details how he used accumulated miles and points to fly his parents to Scotland for a "once-in-a-lifetime" trip. He booked business class flights using United MileagePlus miles, transferred from Chase Ultimate Rewards, and explains how his parents utilized travel benefits, including car rental insurance from the Chase Sapphire Reserve, which proved crucial during their trip.

title: Seventh Circuit Splits With Eleventh on CAFA Jurisdictional Discovery
summary: The Seventh Circuit recently diverged from the Eleventh Circuit regarding the allowance of jurisdictional discovery in cases removed under the Class Action Fairness Act (CAFA). In *Dancel v. Groupon, Inc.*, the Seventh Circuit held that specific allegations of minimal diversity are required and that jurisdictional discovery can be used to prove it, even where the Eleventh Circuit previously prohibited such discovery. This decision is significant for parties arguing federal subject matter jurisdiction under CAFA, particularly in the Seventh Circuit.

title: Will Wells Fargo ever move its headquarters to Charlotte? Its CEO has options.
summary: This article explores the possibility of Wells Fargo moving its headquarters from San Francisco, a city where its headcount has stagnated, to Charlotte, which has seen significant growth in its Wells Fargo employee base. The new CEO, Charlie Scharf, is based in New York City and is initiating foundational changes, raising questions about the bank's future geographic core. Charlotte presents a strong case due to its large employee presence, business-friendly environment, and affordable talent and office space, while San Francisco's high costs and New York's limited headcount make them less ideal for a primary headquarters.

title: Morgan Stanley to Buy Eaton Vance for $7 Billion - WSJ
summary: Morgan Stanley is set to acquire fund manager Eaton Vance Corp. for $7 billion, marking a significant step in the bank's strategy to shift towards more stable businesses like money management. This acquisition follows closely on the heels of its $11 billion takeover of E*Trade Financial Corp., furthering CEO James Gorman's decadelong effort to reduce risky trading operations and bolster wealth and asset management. The deal will nearly double the assets Morgan Stanley manages for institutional clients.

title: Bank of America Profit Falls 16%
summary: Bank of America's profit decreased by 16% in the third quarter, reporting $4.88 billion, though the bank stated it is well-prepared for the coronavirus recession. The bank's provision for loan losses significantly reduced to $1.39 billion, compared to the previous two quarters. Despite the profit fall, CEO Brian Moynihan noted a return to fundamental economic health, contingent on resolving the healthcare crisis.

title: First Citizens to Buy CIT Group
summary: First Citizens BancShares Inc. announced plans to acquire CIT Group Inc. in an all-stock deal valued at approximately $2.2 billion, creating a regional bank with over $100 billion in assets. The new entity will retain the First Citizens name and CEO. This merger aims to strengthen commercial lending by leveraging First Citizens' low-cost deposits, addressing a common challenge for regional banks struggling against larger national competitors and low interest rates.

title: How Hurricane Harvey Led an Army Captain to a Career in Banking
summary: U.S. Army Captain Jake Cortez's experience during Hurricane Harvey, witnessing JPMorgan Chase's community involvement, inspired him to leave the military and join the bank. He became the first in Houston to participate in JPMorgan Chase's Military Pathways Development Program, transitioning into a technology strategist role at the company. This article highlights JPMorgan Chase's commitment to hiring veterans and its investment in technology.

title: Why big banks could be killing private prisons
summary: Private prison companies like CoreCivic and The GEO Group are facing significant challenges despite a boom under the Trump administration. Major banks have started to divest from financing these companies, and public opposition, political pressure, and investor divestment are collectively impacting their stock performance.

title: The Closing: Owen Thomas
summary: This article features an interview with Owen Thomas, CEO of Boston Properties, discussing his career path, including his time at Morgan Stanley and Lehman Brothers, and his leadership of Boston Properties since 2013. He talks about overcoming challenges in succeeding a legendary founder, expanding the company, and his views on the real estate market and co-working spaces. Thomas also shares personal details about his upbringing and hobbies.

title: After Wawa breach, banks reissue thousands of debit, credit cards to customers
summary: Following a data breach that exposed customer payment information at potentially all Wawa stores for nine months, several banks are proactively reissuing debit and credit cards. Citibank is issuing new Wawa-branded credit cards, while Citizens Bank, First National Bank & Trust, and Northfield Bank are reissuing debit cards to affected customers. Wawa has offered customers one year of identity-theft protection and credit monitoring.

title: Goldman Sachs Announces New Business Segments
summary: Goldman Sachs announced new business segments for financial reporting, effective with its Q4 2019 results. The new segments are Investment Banking, Global Markets, Asset Management, and Consumer & Wealth Management, aiming to better reflect the firm's client-centric management and drive accountability. This resegmentation involves reallocating results previously reported under "Investing & Lending" and renaming existing segments.

title: IBM’s Quantum-Computing Service Tops 100 Customers
summary: International Business Machines Corp. announced that its quantum-computing services now have over 100 customers, a significant increase from 40 customers a year ago. These clients include businesses like Delta, Daimler, and JPMorgan, as well as universities and government research facilities. The IBM Q Network, launched in late 2017, provides access to 15 early-stage quantum-computing machines via the cloud, along with developer tools and expert support.

title: ‘We Need to Be a Technology Company.’ Wells Fargo Struggles With Aging Systems.
summary: Wells Fargo is facing challenges with its outdated technology systems, hindering its ability to meet regulatory requirements and impacting key business operations. Despite being a pioneer in online banking, the company has fallen behind in recent years. An incident where a fire-extinguisher system knocked out power to servers, causing an hours-long outage for online and mobile banking, highlights the fragility of their current infrastructure.

title: JPM20: Teladoc to buy enterprise telehealth solutions provider InTouch Health in $600M deal
summary: Teladoc Health announced its intention to acquire InTouch Health for $600 million, consisting of $150 million in cash and $450 million in stock. This acquisition positions Teladoc as a leader in virtual care by integrating InTouch Health's enterprise telehealth solutions for hospitals and health systems. The deal is expected to close by the end of the second quarter and strengthen Teladoc's revenue growth, with InTouch Health projecting $80 million in 2019 revenues.

title: Teladoc to acquire InTouch Health for $600M
summary: Teladoc has agreed to acquire InTouch Health for $600 million, including $150 million in cash and the remainder in common stock. This acquisition aims to boost Teladoc's revenue by roughly $80 million and extend its reach across hospitals and health systems, making it a leader in virtual care across all acuity levels. The deal is expected to close by mid-2020 and will combine Teladoc's consumer presence with InTouch Health's hospital-focused software.

title: Anghami could be up for sale at a value of up to $400m
summary: Anghami, a major music streaming service in the Middle East, is reportedly considering a sale or a new round of investment, potentially valuing the company at up to $400 million. This development comes despite their previous confidence in the face of competition and their expansion into podcasts and video offerings. Orbit Showtime Network is cited as a potential buyer, while JPMorgan Chase & Co. might assist with fundraising.

title: Big Banks Ended 2019 on a High Note (Published 2020)
summary: JPMorgan Chase and Citigroup reported strong financial results for 2019, with JPMorgan achieving record profits. Even Wells Fargo saw positive outcomes despite operational challenges. The success was largely attributed to the 2019 turnaround in financial markets, aided by Federal Reserve rate cuts, which boosted trading revenues for banks.

title: Wells Fargo loses more than 450 advisers in 2019
summary: Wells Fargo Advisors' head count dropped by 456 financial advisers, or 3.3%, in 2019, bringing their total to 13,512. This decline occurred amidst increased expenses for Wells Fargo Advisors and a 63% drop in net income for its Wealth and Investment Management group compared to the previous year. The company's image continues to be affected by past scandals, despite efforts to rebrand.

title: Activists cheer BlackRock's landmark climate move but call for vigilance
summary: BlackRock, the world's biggest asset manager, announced a significant shift in its investment strategy, divesting $500m from coal-related businesses due to climate risks. Environmentalists hailed this as a major breakthrough but urged continued vigilance and further action, emphasizing that these initial steps are just the beginning of necessary changes in the financial sector to combat climate change. Activists and financial experts alike called for BlackRock to leverage its substantial shareholder power to push for immediate, concrete climate actions from companies it invests in.

title: JPM: 'An embarrassment of riches'—Lyndra CEO Hurter on the promise of ultralong-acting pills
summary: Patricia Hurter, former Vertex Pharmaceuticals executive, took over as CEO of Lyndra Therapeutics, a company developing ultralong-acting pills. These pills could revolutionize treatments for chronic diseases by improving adherence and potentially reviving drugs with narrow absorption windows. Lyndra is also focusing on manufacturing scale-up, design tweaks for later-phase studies, and innovative distribution models to ensure affordable access, especially for global health problems.

title: Outgoing Sysco CEO to receive $6M golden parachute
summary: Sysco's outgoing CEO, Tom Bené, is set to receive a $6 million severance payout. His replacement, Kevin Hourican from CVS Pharmacy, will receive a $2 million sign-on bonus, plus "make-whole" bonuses and equity awards totaling over $14 million to compensate for forfeited benefits from his previous employer. This leadership change comes despite Sysco's strong performance under Bené, with the company aiming to accelerate growth further.

title: Japan's MUFG replaces CEO after one year, digital chief to take helm
summary: Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG) announced the replacement of its CEO with its digital chief, Hironori Kamezawa, after just one year, reflecting the bank's urgent push into fintech. This move breaks from tradition as Kamezawa will be the first CEO not to have previously headed the core MUFG Bank. The change highlights Japanese megabanks' efforts to adapt to technological shifts and address low profitability margins compared to global rivals.

title: Nancy Weingard
summary: Nancy Weingard is the Founder and Managing Director of Weingard Wealth Management of Raymond James, providing comprehensive financial planning to affluent individuals, families, and business owners. She is a highly recognized financial advisor, having been featured on Forbes's Best-In-State Wealth Advisors and Top Women Wealth Advisors lists. Weingard emphasizes client education, transparent processes, and a multidisciplinary approach to wealth management, holding CFP®, CLTC, and AEP® certifications.

title: Fifth Third customer gets $250 for opening an account, then receives tax form in the mail: Money Matters
summary: A Fifth Third Bank customer received a $250 bonus for opening an account and was surprised to get a 1099-INT tax form, making the bonus taxable income. The article clarifies that cash incentives from banks are considered interest income and are reportable to the IRS. It also addresses an unrelated reader question about doctors' offices requiring a credit card on file, offering a solution using a prepaid debit card for anonymity.

title: BMO Harris hires two execs away from rival Fifth Third
summary: BMO Harris Bank has hired Eric Smith and Michael Morton from Fifth Third Bancorp to bolster its commercial banking division. Both Smith and Morton, who previously held key roles at Fifth Third and MB Financial respectively, will report to David Casper, U.S. chief executive at BMO Harris, as the bank aims to expand its commercial lending nationwide.

title: Michael A. Nicolas, CFA
summary: This article provides a professional profile of Michael A. Nicolas, CFA, a Partner and Portfolio Manager at Harris Associates, advisor to the Oakmark Funds. It details his professional history, the funds he manages (Oakmark Fund, Oakmark Equity and Income Fund, and Oakmark U.S. Large Cap ETF), and highlights recent commentaries and news featuring him. The article also touches upon the investment philosophy of Oakmark, emphasizing long-term value investing.

title: The Top 15 high-paying employers in Denver with the most open jobs
summary: Denver, Colorado, a recently ranked "boomtown" for its economic growth and job abundance, is attracting numerous job seekers. This article identifies the top 15 companies hiring for over $100,000 jobs in Denver, with Cognizant Technology Solutions leading the list with 857 open positions, followed by Comcast and Infosys.

title: Philadelphia firm, JPMorgan team on $300M venture to buy often-overlooked real estate
summary: Alterra Property Group has secured $300 million for a new joint venture with JPMorgan Chase. This partnership aims to acquire often-overlooked real estate assets. The venture signifies a notable investment in a specific property type by a Philadelphia firm and a major financial institution.

title: Exelon Generation buys Kennett Square buildings
summary: Exelon Generation Co. has acquired a two-building office campus in Kennett Square, Pennsylvania. The company, located in the two buildings along Exelon Way, completed the transaction for the 249,090-square-foot property. This purchase signifies Exelon Generation's continued presence and investment in the region.

title: Forbes ranks First Merchants Bank among top 5 banks in U.S. for 3rd straight year
summary: Forbes has ranked First Merchants Bank as the fifth best bank in the United States for the third consecutive year, based on their 2020 "America's Best Banks" list. The bank, which was rated second in 2019 and fourth in 2018, outranked major financial institutions like JPMorgan Chase and Citigroup. Forbes assesses banks based on 10 metrics including growth, profitability, capital adequacy, and asset quality.

title: Fifth Third Bank names Nick Buzzelli its next Akron president
summary: Fifth Third Bank has appointed Nick Buzzelli as its new Akron president, a role that also encompasses the Canton and Youngstown regions. Buzzelli, currently a senior vice president, will succeed Ted Walter, who retires on March 31. He previously worked at Citizens Bank and Huntington Bank and is a University of Akron graduate.

title: One of Pittsburgh's biggest banks cutting 15 branches
summary: F.N.B. Corp., one of Pittsburgh's largest banks, is set to close 15 branches, adding to the trend of branch closures. This early 2020 tally already accounts for 60% of the total closures seen in 2019. The move includes the relocation of the Mount Washington office into the South Side branch, formerly Iron & Glass Bank.

title: Will Value Stocks Overtake Growth Stocks In 2020?
summary: The article discusses whether value stocks will outperform growth stocks in 2020, following a decade of underperformance for value investing. It highlights billionaire investor Seth Klarman's perspective on market mispricings favoring value and references Bank of America's expectations for accelerating profit growth, which historically benefits value stocks. The piece also suggests relevant ETFs for investors interested in this trend.

title: Victory Capital HQ Settles Into Former USAA Offices at La Cantera
summary: Victory Capital Holdings, a global investment company, relocated its corporate headquarters from Cleveland, Ohio, to San Antonio, occupying former USAA offices at La Cantera. This move followed its $850 million acquisition of USAA's asset management company, with leadership citing San Antonio's potential for long-term growth and its talent pool. The company currently employs 150 employees in San Antonio and manages $152 billion in assets.

title: Goldman Sachs Investor Day: ‘Embracing the bank model,’ but which bank?
summary: Goldman Sachs held its first-ever Investor Day, outlining ambitious goals to expand its consumer banking, transaction services, and wealth management, aiming for significant deposit and loan growth by 2025. Despite these growth initiatives, the event was largely met with a lack of excitement from investors and analysts, who noted concern over the risk associated with new revenue streams and compared Goldman's new strategy to that of commercial banks like Citigroup or JPMorgan. The bank also detailed cost-cutting measures and targets to boost its return on tangible equity, though its stock performance since October 2018 lagged competitors.

title: As Voya Financial sells off insurance groups, attention turns to its broker-dealer
summary: Voya Financial's broker-dealer, Voya Financial Advisors, is facing questions about its future as the parent company divests its insurance businesses. Industry experts suggest the broker-dealer, with 1,700 advisers, could be the next unit up for sale, especially given recent private equity acquisitions in the sector. Voya Financial has publicly stated its intention to focus on retirement, investment management, and employee benefits, with the broker-dealer operating under its retirement group.

title: Westrock Coffee Co to acquire S&D Coffee & Tea
summary: Westrock Coffee Company, LLC has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire S&D Coffee & Tea from Cott Corporation, a transaction expected to close within weeks. This acquisition will create a leading integrated coffee company serving retail, restaurant, convenience store, and hospitality industries, leveraging the strengths of both organizations. The combined entity will employ approximately 1,700 people globally and aims to be a premier supplier of coffee, tea, and extracts with a focus on sustainability and innovation.

title: 20 questions for Rick Van Nieuwenhuyse
summary: Rick Van Nieuwenhuyse, CEO of Contango ORE, discusses his new role, the Peak Gold project in Alaska, and his vision for expanding Contango into an exploration powerhouse. He shares insights on community engagement, the challenges and opportunities of operating a mineral exploration company listed on the Pink Sheets, the potential for new gold discoveries in Alaska, and the future of the junior exploration market and metal prices.

title: Goldman Sachs in talks with Amazon to offer small-business loans
summary: Goldman Sachs is reportedly close to a deal with Amazon to offer small-business loans to Amazon's U.S. customers, aiming to expand its reach onto Main Street. This move aligns with Goldman's strategy to diversify beyond trading and investment banking, while Amazon benefits by extending its lending platform without incurring significant credit risk or regulatory obligations. The partnership would leverage Goldman's financial services expertise and Amazon's vast network of small and medium-sized sellers, further solidifying both companies' ventures into new market segments.

title: Remitly Launches Passbook – Banking Designed for Immigrants
summary: Remitly has launched Passbook, a new banking solution specifically designed for immigrants in the U.S. Passbook offers an online, no-fee account that eliminates common barriers to financial services, such as the need for a social security number, and includes immigrant-friendly features like global usability and customizable Visa Debit Cards. The service aims to transform banking for the over 44 million first-generation adult immigrants in the U.S., building on Remitly's mission to support this community.

title: Chase, Old National bank branches to close in Muncie and Yorktown
summary: Old National Bank and Chase Bank are closing several branches in Muncie and Yorktown, Indiana, due to a significant shift towards online and mobile banking. Old National Bank's branch at 2700 W. Jackson St. will close on April 24, consolidating with its downtown location, while Chase's Yorktown branch at 9213 W. Smith St. will close on May 5, consolidating with the Tillotson Square branch. Despite the closures, both banks acknowledge the continued importance of physical branches for customer advice, with Chase noting that one million customers still use their branches weekly.

title: Beam Therapeutics shines in $180m IPO
summary: Beam Therapeutics, a genomic medicine developer backed by Alphabet, Editas, and Bio Palette, successfully completed an upsized $180 million IPO, pricing shares at $17.00. The company increased its share offering to nearly 10.6 million and plans to use the proceeds to fund R&D, clinical trials, and drug discovery. Previously, Beam Therapeutics secured significant funding rounds from investors including GV, Eight Roads Ventures, F-Prime Capital, Hillhouse Capital, Temasek, and Arch Venture Partners, which was its largest pre-IPO shareholder.

title: Exclusive: Goldman Sachs to raise $8 billion for new buyout fund - sources
summary: Goldman Sachs Group Inc is reportedly planning to raise $8 billion for a new buyout fund, its second since the 2008 financial crisis, to bolster its global deal-making capabilities. The fundraising, to be launched by its private equity arm West Street Capital Partners, aims for a first close by the end of March, primarily targeting offshore investors despite the coronavirus epidemic. This new fund underscores Goldman's commitment to the private equity business, focusing on deals where it gains majority control, with 60% of capital deployed in America and about 25 investments ranging from $150 million to $600 million each.

title: UH Computer Science Students Dominate Code for Good
summary: University of Houston computer science students excelled at JPMorgan Chase's "Code for Good" hackathon, where they developed applications for non-profit organizations. Several UH students, including Vyas Ramankulangara and Jesus Del Riego, placed highly in the competition, securing internships and full-time job offers with JPMorgan Chase. The event provided valuable experience working with new people and applying their skills to real-world problems for social good.

title: Mike Weinbach to Join Wells Fargo to lead Consumer Lending
summary: Wells Fargo announced that Mike Weinbach will join the company in early May as CEO of Consumer Lending, reporting to CEO Charlie Scharf. Weinbach will oversee Home Lending, Auto, Credit Cards & Merchant Services, and Personal Loans. He brings 16 years of experience from JPMorgan Chase, where he most recently led Chase Home Lending.

title: Global Financial Giants Swear Off Funding an Especially Dirty Fuel (Published 2020)
summary: Major financial institutions, including The Hartford, Sweden's central bank, and BlackRock, have begun divesting from oil production in the Canadian province of Alberta's oil sands due to environmental concerns. This move highlights a growing trend among global investment houses to pull away from fossil fuel investments amid pressure to combat climate change. While foreign investors are withdrawing, local Canadian banks and pension funds continue to support the industry, and some divesting companies still invest in oil projects elsewhere.

title: Wells Fargo splits wholesale, consumer banking units
summary: Wells Fargo is undergoing a significant restructuring, splitting its three business units into five to enhance accountability under CEO Charlie Scharf. The wholesale bank will be divided into commercial and investment banking units, while the consumer bank will split into branches/small businesses and consumer lending arms. This overhaul aims to flatten the organizational structure and address past regulatory issues and a damaged reputation.

title: iStar Announces Jeremy Fox-Geen as New Chief Financial Officer
summary: iStar Inc. announced Jeremy Fox-Geen will join as Chief Financial Officer for both iStar and Safehold at the end of March 2020. Mr. Fox-Geen brings over 20 years of experience in corporate finance and financial services, previously serving as CFO of McKinsey & Co.'s North American business. He will report to Jay Sugarman, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, and oversee Accounting, Tax, Treasury, and Investor Relations.

title: Radian Adds Two New Directors
summary: Radian Group Inc. has appointed Lisa Mumford and Brad Conner to its board of directors, bringing extensive C-suite experience in finance, accounting, and mortgage lending. Mumford previously served as CFO for Ellington Financial Inc. and Ellington Residential Mortgage REIT, while Conner was the vice chairman of Consumer Banking at Citizens Financial Group Inc. and president of JP Morgan Chase & Company’s Home Equity business. David Carney, a director since 1992, plans to retire from the board.

title: Revolution hits public markets in $238m IPO
summary: Precision cancer therapy developer Revolution Medicines raised $238m in an IPO on the Nasdaq Global Market, with shares rising 70% on their first day of trading. The IPO also provided an exit for pharmaceutical company Sanofi, a significant shareholder. Proceeds from the IPO will fund the development of oncology drug candidates, particularly those targeting the Ras protein pathway.

title: Green Bay financial services firm to acquire Commerce State Bank
summary: Nicolet National Bank, a Green Bay financial services firm, is expected to acquire Commerce State Bank. The transaction is projected to close in the third quarter of the year. This acquisition will expand Nicolet National Bank's presence, integrating Commerce State Bank's operations.

title: KeyCorp names Victor Alexander head of consumer banking
summary: KeyCorp has appointed Victor Alexander as executive vice president and head of Key Consumer Bank, succeeding Dennis Devine. Alexander, who joined Key in 2000, previously led the home lending division and served as corporate treasurer. In his new role, he will oversee various consumer banking lines of business and will join KeyCorp's Executive Leadership Team.

title: Subi Sethi Joins Clearwater as Chief Client Officer
summary: Clearwater Analytics announced that Subi Sethi has joined the company as Chief Client Officer, responsible for leading the firm’s global operations team. Sethi brings extensive experience in driving operational transformation and will oversee Global Delivery, Data, Reconciliation, Client Services, and Strategic Account Management teams. Her focus will include uniting and creating efficiencies across Clearwater's international offices to strengthen global servicing capabilities.

title: Global Partners Selling 18 Convenience Stores
summary: Global Partners LP is selling 18 convenience stores with gasoline across Vermont, New Hampshire, and Rhode Island. These properties, ranging from 900 to 3,100 square feet, include both operating and closed sites, some with minimal competition. NRC Realty & Capital Advisors LLC is managing the sealed-bid sale process, with bids due by April 16, 2020.

title: Franklin exits fund purgatory with Legg Mason deal
summary: Franklin Resources Inc. is acquiring Legg Mason Inc. for nearly $4.5 billion, a move that will double Franklin's assets and create a $1.5 billion asset-management firm. This acquisition is seen as Franklin's strategy to regain its position as a leader in active management after a period of stagnant growth and a credit rating downgrade, positioning itself to better compete in a consolidating industry. The deal is also intended to address future trends in the industry, such as ActiveShares ETFs, where Franklin previously lagged.

title: Franklin Matchmaker in $1.5 Trillion Deal Was Legg Mason Adviser
summary: The article details how Matthew Nicholls, CFO of Franklin Resources, played a pivotal role in brokering the $1.5 trillion deal between Franklin Resources Inc. and Legg Mason Inc. Nicholls leveraged his prior experience as an investment banker for Legg Mason to understand both companies, facilitating the acquisition. The combined entity still boasts $5 billion in cash for future strategic purchases.

title: WFW advises on US$3bn Taiwanese offshore wind farm project financing
summary: Watson Farley & Williams (WFW) advised a large syndicate of international and Taiwanese financial institutions on the project financing of the US$3bn Changfang and Xidao Taiwanese offshore wind projects. This financing, which will fund the construction of a 600 MW wind farm, is the largest debt package raised in the Taiwanese offshore wind market to date. The transaction involved complex, multi-tranche, multi-currency financing arrangements, including support from various export credit agencies.

title: Wells Fargo to pay $3 billion to U.S., admits pressuring workers in fake-accounts scandal
summary: Wells Fargo has agreed to pay $3 billion to resolve criminal and civil probes into fraudulent sales practices, admitting to pressuring employees in a fake-accounts scandal. The settlement, which includes penalties to the U.S. Justice Department and SEC, marks a significant step for the bank in moving past the scandal. The bank acknowledged that between 2002 and 2016, employees were coerced to meet unrealistic sales goals, leading to millions of unauthorized accounts.

title: JPMorgan Chase in talks to launch digital bank in UK
summary: JPMorgan Chase is reportedly in talks with London regulators to launch a digital bank in the UK by the end of the year. This move could significantly impact the UK retail banking market, following Goldman Sachs' successful launch of its digital bank, Marcus, two years prior. The new operation is expected to offer savings and lending products and represents a notable international expansion for Chase, especially as other banks consider shifting operations due to Brexit.

title: FEI and Robert Half
summary: FEI and Robert Half co-hosted their third "Intern Night" on February 19, 2020, bringing together students from various universities with financial professionals. The event featured a panel discussion and provided students with networking opportunities and a chance to submit resumes for internships. Panelists included representatives from MedVet, KeyBank, ms consultants, and Schneider Downs.

title: JPMorgan Chase to stop loans for fossil fuel drilling in the Arctic
summary: JPMorgan Chase announced it will stop approving loans for new fossil fuel drilling in the Arctic Circle, following similar actions by Goldman Sachs and pressure from environmental groups and lawmakers. The bank also committed to completing $200 billion in clean energy financing and sourcing renewable energy for its needs by year-end, while phasing out loans to companies predominantly involved in coal mining by 2024. Environmental groups offered mixed reactions, noting limitations in the coal policy and the lack of restrictions on oil and gas financing outside the Arctic.

title: How JPMorgan Chase Became the Doomsday Bank
summary: JPMorgan Chase is identified as the largest lender to the fossil-fuel industry globally, having lent $196 billion since the Paris Agreement. The article details the bank's historical ties to fossil fuels and its CEO Jamie Dimon's public statements on climate change versus the bank's substantial investments in environmentally damaging projects. It highlights a national campaign of civil disobedience aimed at forcing Chase to change its course, noting potential opportunities for change at the bank's annual investor day.

title: JPMorgan won’t finance new Arctic drilling, most coal plants
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. announced it will no longer finance new Arctic drilling projects and will further restrict investments in coal companies. The banking giant also committed $200 billion to the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals, including $50 billion for green initiatives. This move comes amid growing pressure from investors and environmental groups on financial institutions to divest from fossil fuels.

title: Revealed: The top three global high yield fund managers
summary: Citywire Selector has identified the top three global high yield fund managers based on their three-year total returns ending January 2020. Michael Scott of Man GLG secured the top spot, followed by Eric Holt and Rachid Semaoune of Royal London Asset Management, and Andrew Jackson of HSBC. The article details their performance, asset allocation, and fund specifics.

title: BRT Apartments Pays $38M for North Carolina Community
summary: BRT Apartments Corp. has acquired Abbotts Run, a 264-unit community in Wilmington, N.C., for $38 million, financed with a $23.2 million Fannie Mae loan. The company plans capital improvements for the 95.8 percent occupied property, which marks BRT's second acquisition in North Carolina.

title: JPMorgan Will Stop Lending to Coal Companies
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. announced it will cease doing business with coal companies and restrict financing for Arctic drilling projects. The bank plans to phase out existing coal company loans by 2024 and will only fund new coal-powered plants that include carbon capture technology. This move comes as JPMorgan also committed $200 billion in financing for clean and renewable energy companies by 2025.

title: JP Morgan Chase Commits $200 Billion to Sustainability Financing
summary: JPMorgan Chase has announced a commitment of $200 billion in financing for sustainability goals this year, including restrictions on lending to coal mining and the cessation of direct funding for Arctic drilling projects. This move mirrors similar pledges by European banks and Goldman Sachs, though some climate activists argue the targets may not be sufficient to align with Paris Agreement goals. The bank also reiterated its 2017 clean financing target of $200 billion by 2025 and its commitment to renewable energy by this year.

title: Capital One is closing dozens of branches — and some are local
summary: Capital One is closing dozens more branches, including some local ones, as it continues to shrink its physical footprint. This move comes as the bank has embraced a smaller branch network, exemplified by its Cafe concept.

title: Eileen Serra to Join the Capital One Board of Directors
summary: Capital One Financial Corporation announced the appointment of Eileen Serra to its Board of Directors, effective February 26, 2020. Ms. Serra, former Chase Credit Card CEO, brings over two decades of experience in the financial services industry, including leadership roles at JP Morgan Chase, Merrill Lynch, American Express, and McKinsey & Company. Her expertise in product development, digital transformation, and strategic growth is expected to significantly contribute to Capital One's mission of reimagining banking.

title: New JPMorgan Chase CMO has come a long way from telesales gig
summary: Leslie Gillin has been appointed as the new Chief Marketing Officer (CMO) at JPMorgan Chase, capping a 30-year career that began in telemarketing at MBNA America. In her new role, Gillin oversees marketing for the Chase, JPMorgan Chase & Co., and J.P. Morgan brands, emphasizing customer-centric strategies, data leverage, and strategic partnerships. She plans to focus on aligning marketing goals with business objectives, enhancing ROI on marketing spend, and optimizing omnichannel targeting.

title: Hourly bleach may follow travel bans at banks
summary: Big banks globally are preparing for a potential coronavirus pandemic by implementing measures like travel bans, hourly sanitization, and splitting teams to maintain operations. Consulting firms are advising clients, including major financial institutions, to refine their continuity plans for potential office closures and staff disruptions. These steps are being taken to ensure financial markets remain functional even as the virus spreads, with some banks already adopting split-team strategies abroad.

title: Why Morgan Stanley is buying E-Trade
summary: Morgan Stanley is acquiring E-Trade for $13 billion to expand its wealth management business and attract a broader base of middle-class investors and digital natives. This acquisition allows Morgan Stanley to diversify its revenue streams beyond traditional trading and compete with rivals like Goldman Sachs in serving emerging wealth segments. The move reflects a long-term bet on the increasing wealth of the middle class and a shift towards digital financial services.

title: Dividend Growth Investing Made Easy with ETFs
summary: This article, a guest post by Tom of Dividends Diversify, explains how dividend growth investing can be made easy through the use of Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs). It highlights the benefits of diversification offered by ETFs and discusses several popular dividend ETFs such as VYM, VIG, VYMI, and NOBL, outlining their characteristics and investment strategies. The article also touches on considerations for Canadian investors regarding withholding taxes and briefly mentions individual stock holdings.

title: Banking vet Mitch Feiger stepping down as Fifth Third Chicago chair
summary: Mitch Feiger, chair of the Chicago region for Fifth Third Bancorp and former CEO of MB Financial, is stepping down to join the bank's board. He will be succeeded by Mark Hoppe, who was his second-in-command at MB Financial.
