This change comes after Fifth Third's acquisition of MB Financial, a move that significantly boosted Fifth Third's presence in the Chicago market.

title: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon has emergency heart surgery
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. CEO Jamie Dimon underwent emergency heart surgery for an acute aortic dissection. Co-Presidents Daniel Pinto and Gordon Smith will lead the bank during his recuperation. Dimon, 63, is the longest-serving head of a major U.S. bank and previously battled throat cancer in 2014.

title: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon undergoes emergency heart surgery
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. CEO Jamie Dimon underwent emergency heart surgery on Thursday for an acute aortic dissection, according to a memo sent to employees. Dimon, 63, is recovering well, and co-presidents Daniel Pinto and Gordon Smith will oversee the bank during his recuperation. This event highlights Dimon's long tenure as the leader of the largest U.S. bank since 2005.

title: JPMorgan Chief Executive Jamie Dimon Has Emergency Heart Surgery (Published 2020)
summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon underwent successful emergency heart surgery for an acute aortic dissection after experiencing chest pains. While he recovers, senior executives Daniel Pinto and Gordon Smith will lead the bank. Dimon, known for his long tenure and resilience through financial crises, has overseen JPMorgan's growth into the largest U.S. bank.

title: Fifth Third opened fake accounts like Wells Fargo, government says
summary: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) has filed a lawsuit against Fifth Third Bank, alleging that its employees opened fake accounts to meet aggressive sales targets, similar to Wells Fargo's past misconduct. The CFPB claims Fifth Third knew about these practices from at least 2008 to 2016. Fifth Third, however, stated that an internal investigation found only 1,100 fraudulently opened accounts out of 10 million and minimal financial damage.

title: Fifth Third employees opened fake accounts to meet sales goals, US government says
summary: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) has filed a lawsuit alleging that Fifth Third Bank employees opened fake accounts to meet aggressive sales goals, mirroring practices seen at Wells Fargo. Fifth Third Bank denies the allegations, stating their compensation structure does not reward unauthorized accounts and that they had already identified and addressed a small number of fraudulent accounts internally. The bank also asserted that the CFPB did not identify any additional fake accounts beyond what their internal investigation uncovered.

title: Thermo Fisher Scientific Names Paul G. Parker to Head Strategy and Corporate Development
summary: Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. announced the appointment of Paul G. Parker as senior vice president, strategy and corporate development, effective April 15, 2020. Parker joins from Goldman Sachs & Co. with 35 years of investment banking experience. He will report to Marc N. Casper, and his role will also encompass corporate social responsibility.

title: JPMorgan’s Global CIO Talks Emerging Tech, Top Talent, and Honing in on DFW
summary: JPMorgan Chase's Global CIO, Lori Beer, discusses the company's deep integration of technology, its significant investment in emerging tech like AI and machine learning, and its focus on attracting and retaining top tech talent in regions like Dallas-Fort Worth. She highlights JPMorgan's commitment to continuous learning through programs like PowerUp and community involvement, emphasizing DFW's critical role in the company's overall strategy due to its growing tech ecosystem and talent pool. Beer also touches on the firm's efforts in diversity and inclusion within its technology workforce.

title: Royal Bank of Canada says employee in Manhattan tested positive for coronavirus
summary: Royal Bank of Canada announced that an employee in its investment banking division in lower Manhattan tested positive for coronavirus, leading to the employee and close contacts self-quarantining and a deep clean of the affected area. This is the third known case for RBC, following two employees in a suburban Toronto office, and adds the bank to a growing list of financial firms reporting cases as the pandemic spreads globally. The World Health Organization declared the outbreak a pandemic on the same day.

title: As Wall Street dives, what’s the plan at Wells Fargo Advisors?
summary: The article discusses how Wells Fargo Advisors is trying to navigate an intense market sell-off and emerge from past scandals, contrasting its situation with competitors Merrill Lynch and Morgan Stanley. Despite challenges and adviser departures, Wells Fargo Advisors' new leadership aims to focus on financial planning, banking referrals, and leveraging the parent bank's strengths to find new clients, similar to strategies employed by its rivals. The piece highlights the scrutiny new CEO Charles Scharf and president Jim Hays will face as they try to make up for lost time amid a bear market.

title: Long dormant PayPal Credit accounts are coming back to haunt users—and hurt their credit scores
summary: Many PayPal Credit users are experiencing unexpected drops in their credit scores due to accounts, some long dormant or unknown, now being reported to credit bureaus by Synchrony Bank. This change, which began in October linked to a 2018 switch in credit issuers from Comenity Bank to Synchrony, has caught many account holders off guard, claiming they received no notification. The situation has led to confusion, frustration, and significant credit score impacts for individuals like Mike Fitzpatrick and Caitlyn Rose, prompting questions about PayPal's communication and past practices.

title: JPMorgan, Bank of America, Citigroup and other major banks suspend stock buybacks due to pandemic
summary: Major U.S. banks including JPMorgan, Bank of America, and Citigroup announced they would suspend stock buybacks through the second quarter of 2020 due to the coronavirus pandemic. This decision, made by members of the Financial Services Forum, aims to preserve capital and liquidity to support individuals, small businesses, and the broader economy through lending and other services during the "unprecedented challenge." Bank stocks have seen significant declines since the start of 2020 as the virus spread globally.

title: Biggest U.S. Banks Halt Buybacks to Free Up Capital for Coronavirus
summary: The biggest U.S. banks have temporarily suspended share buybacks to free up capital, aiming to support consumers and businesses impacted by the rapid economic slowdown caused by the novel coronavirus outbreak. This decision was announced by the Financial Services Forum shortly after the Federal Reserve reduced its benchmark interest rate to near zero. The move underscores the financial industry's response to an "unprecedented challenge" posed by the pandemic to the global economy.

title: JPMorgan Chase, Nationwide Insurance telling more employees to work from home
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Nationwide Insurance are instructing more of their employees to work from home. This move is part of a broader trend as companies respond to current conditions. The article highlights the decisions made by these large employers in Columbus.

title: Huntington Bank CEO: The banking system is safe
summary: Steve Steinour, CEO of Huntington Bank, affirmed the banking system's safety amidst the coronavirus pandemic, instructing his executive team to maintain their course. This directive comes even as other financial institutions like JPMorgan Chase and Nationwide Insurance are sending employees home and Ohio banks are offering consumer relief.

title: Horizon Bank puts Safety First to Assist in the Effort to Reduce the Spread of Covid-19 – Lobbies Open by Appointment Only
summary: Horizon Bank announced that effective March 19, 2020, all branch lobbies in Indiana and Michigan would be open by appointment only to prioritize the safety of customers and employees amidst the COVID-19 pandemic. The bank continues to offer services through drive-ups, ATMs, Live Video Banking, online, and mobile banking. Customers are encouraged to call their local branch for appointments or utilize alternative banking options.

title: 2019 Annual Report
summary: Goldman Sachs' 2019 Annual Report details the firm's financial performance of $36.55 billion in net revenues and a 10.0% return on average common shareholders’ equity, alongside a strategic outlook for growth and increased efficiency. The report highlights the firm's commitment to core values, diversity, and sustainability, while acknowledging the profound impact and uncertainty caused by the COVID-19 pandemic on the global economy. David M. Solomon emphasizes the firm's resilience, client focus, and ongoing efforts to strengthen existing businesses and invest in new opportunities.

title: Citigroup is giving some employees a $1,000 bonus for working through the coronavirus pandemic
summary: Citigroup announced it is giving a $1,000 bonus to some employees, particularly those earning $60,000 or less, to help ease the financial burden of working during the coronavirus pandemic. This initiative will provide special compensation to over 75,000 colleagues globally and applies to various roles including tellers and call center workers. The bank is also offering other support such as paid time off flexibility and transportation assistance for site-dependent staff.

title: Fed announces unlimited bond purchases in unprecedented move aimed at preventing an economic depression
summary: The Federal Reserve announced an unprecedented move to make unlimited bond purchases to prevent an economic depression caused by the coronavirus outbreak. This effort aims to keep money flowing to companies, households, and cities, addressing the severe disruption expected in the economy. The Fed's actions are designed to support the economy as the crisis threatens to surpass the Great Recession.

title: Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd. (RCL) Bolsters Liquidity
summary: Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd. (RCL) has secured a $2.2 billion 364-day secured term loan to significantly enhance its liquidity, bringing its total liquidity to over $3.6 billion. This financial move comes as the cruise industry faces unprecedented disruption, with RCL having suspended all cruises from U.S. ports for 30 days. The company expects to resume service on April 11 and remains focused on protecting its financial position and long-term plans.

title: Coronavirus causing 'unprecedented' US dollar strength
summary: Despite a recent weekly decline, the U.S. dollar continues to show unprecedented strength early in the current recession, driven by its role as a safe-haven asset amidst global economic turmoil caused by COVID-19. Analysts at JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Bank of America suggest further upside for the dollar, citing historical recessionary strength and bullish technical indicators, despite its recent dip and coordinated central bank actions to provide dollar liquidity.

title: JPMorgan Announces New Diversity Push
summary: JPMorgan Chase announced new initiatives to diversify its workforce and customer base after a New York Times report highlighted instances of racism and lack of opportunity for Black customers and employees. The bank is making diversity training mandatory for all employees, expanding its recruiting team for people of color, and re-evaluating how customers qualify for perks. These changes come amidst pressure from lawmakers and advocacy groups following the initial report.

title: Target Issues Bonds to Raise $2.5B
summary: Minneapolis-based retailer Target Corp. issued $2.5 billion in bonds on Tuesday to bolster its balance sheet amid the economic uncertainty caused by Covid-19. The bonds were offered in two blocks: $1.5 billion due in 2025 at 2.25% interest and $1 billion due in 2030 at 2.65% interest, with nine institutional investors pledging to buy them. This move aligns with a broader trend of companies borrowing record amounts in the investment-grade bond market to build cash reserves.

title: Morgan Stanley's CEO says downturn is 'exactly the kind of reason' for E-Trade deal
summary: Morgan Stanley CEO James Gorman stated that the recent market downturn validates the bank's acquisition of E-Trade, emphasizing the online broker's robust technology and the deal's ability to diversify Morgan Stanley's revenue streams toward more stable wealth management. He noted that E-Trade handled the rapid market pullback "brilliantly" and provides crucial technological capabilities, especially as more people deal remotely. Gorman expressed satisfaction with the all-stock deal, despite both companies' stock price movements since the February 20th announcement.

title: Associated Bank, Town Bank work with EDBC on grants for small businesses harmed by COVID-19
summary: Associated Bank is joining Town Bank in providing relief grants to small businesses through the Ethnic and Diverse Business Coalition to help those impacted by COVID-19. To qualify, businesses must have an annual income under $1 million and be a member in good standing with one of the chambers. This initiative aims to support local small businesses facing financial difficulties during the pandemic.

title: Wan Razly said to be top contender for Affin Bank CEO
summary: Wan Razly Abdullah of CIMB Group is reportedly the top contender for the CEO position at Affin Bank Bhd, succeeding Kamarul Ariffin Mohd Jamil whose contract expires soon. His appointment is pending Bank Negara Malaysia's approval. This leadership change aligns with efforts to revitalize the bank, which appointed a new chairman last year and seeks fresh ideas amidst challenging economic conditions.

title: Valley National Bank Among Banks Investigated for Improper Overdraft Fee Practices
summary: Valley National Bank is among several financial institutions under investigation for allegedly improper overdraft fee practices. The article details how overdraft fees work, ways consumers can avoid them, and deceptive practices banks may use, such as reordering transactions or displaying inaccurate online balances. Consumers who believe they have been subject to improper overdraft fees are encouraged to seek legal consultation.

title: What Have We Learned So Far About ETFs In The COVID-19 Crisis? – The FinReg Blog
summary: The article examines the performance and implications of Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) during the COVID-19 financial crisis. It highlights fragilities such as significant discounts to Net Asset Value (NAV), questions the stability of arbitrage mechanisms, and discusses the Federal Reserve's unprecedented intervention in the corporate credit ETF market, raising concerns about the systemic importance of large asset managers like BlackRock. The piece also debates whether ETFs passed a "stress test" or simply benefited from federal bailout, and the potential long-term consequences of such interventions.

title: Moody's places IndusInd Bank's issuer ratings on review for downgrade
summary: Moody's Investors Service has placed IndusInd Bank Ltd’s domestic and foreign currency issuer ratings under review for downgrade due to risks to asset quality stemming from the deteriorating macroenvironment and financial market volatility. The review reflects concerns over the bank's higher proportion of microfinance and vehicle finance loans, which are vulnerable to economic shocks, and its weaker funding compared to peers. Moody's also revised outlooks for ICICI Bank and Axis Bank to negative from stable, and for IDBI Bank to stable from positive, citing a negative outlook for the Indian banking system due to the COVID-19 outbreak.

title: Barrick paid CEO Bristow US$17.4-million in 2019
summary: Barrick Gold Corp. paid CEO Mark Bristow US$17.4-million in 2019, making it one of the largest compensation packages ever awarded by the company. His pay included a salary, share awards, and a bonus, while executive chairman John Thornton received US$5.5-million. The total compensation for Barrick's top five executives reached US$39.44-million, and shareholders will vote on executive pay at an upcoming virtual annual meeting.

title: Biggest Gainers of Rise in India’s Weight on MSCI EM Index
summary: India's weight on the MSCI EM Index is set to increase by 0.55%, potentially attracting over $7 billion in inflows into Indian equities. This rebalancing by MSCI, driven by an increase in foreign investment limits, is expected to benefit specific large-cap stocks like Larsen & Toubro, Asian Paints, and Bajaj Finance, among others. The article highlights Morgan Stanley's analysis of the potential capital influx and the biggest beneficiaries of this change, which could help erase losses from previous FII outflows.

title: TD Bank sees remote work in new light amid 9,500-employee transition
summary: TD Bank is shifting the majority of its 9,500 call center employees to work from home due to the coronavirus crisis, aiming to complete the transition by the end of April 2020. This move marks a significant change for the bank, which initially couldn't imagine such a conversion, and may lead to a permanent work-from-home option for agents due to increased flexibility. Alongside the transition, the bank is offering bonuses and additional personal days to support essential workers and those managing daycare issues.

title: Fifth Third deluged with 33K paycheck protection loan applications
summary: Fifth Third Bank, which typically processes 300 SBA loans annually, received approximately 33,000 applications for the Paycheck Protection Program Loan in about a week. CEO Greg Carmichael described the process as "daunting" due to program details being finalized late and the SBA computer system struggling with demand. Despite the challenges, Carmichael expressed confidence in banks navigating the situation and in additional funds being approved for the program.

title: Private Banks Owning Oil Companies Is A Recipe for Disaster
summary: Major US banks like JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, and Citigroup are reportedly seeking regulatory approval to directly own oil and gas companies, a move criticized by environmental organizations. Critics argue this contradicts the banks' climate commitments and risks further environmental damage and corruption, especially if using federal bailout money. Organizations are urging Congress and regulators to prevent banks from owning fossil fuel assets and to ensure bailout funds are tied to fossil fuel phase-out.

title: JPMorgan shares drop after bank warns borrower defaults could get 'meaningfully' worse
summary: JPMorgan Chase reported first-quarter profit significantly below analysts' expectations, driven by a massive $6.8 billion addition to credit reserves in anticipation of a surge in borrower defaults due to the coronavirus pandemic. Despite this, the bank's revenue held up relatively well, with its trading division posting a record 32% increase in revenue. CFO Jennifer Piepszak warned that future reserve builds for defaults could be "meaningfully higher" in the coming quarters.

title: Square and PayPal finally have a chance to prove they can beat the banks
summary: Fintech companies like PayPal, Square, and Intuit have been approved by the SBA to distribute Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loans, presenting a significant opportunity. BTIG analyst Mark Palmer believes this allows them to demonstrate their superior speed and reach compared to traditional banks in lending to small businesses during the COVID-19 crisis. This designation is seen as the chance these fintech firms have been awaiting to prove their capabilities.

title: Key Numbers From JPMorgan Chase & Co (JPM) Q1 2020 Earnings Results
summary: JPMorgan Chase (JPM) reported a 71% decline in Q1 2020 EPS, with net income at $2.86 billion or $0.78 per share due to a significant increase in credit loss provisions (up $6.8 billion to $8.3 billion) mainly from the COVID-19 impact and oil price pressure. Despite the earnings drop, JPM shares gained over 3% following the announcement, and CEO Jamie Dimon affirmed the company's strong capital position and liquidity to navigate the crisis.

title: Subprime stocks drop $7B in market cap since March
summary: Five subprime auto lenders have seen their market capitalization collectively drop by $7 billion since early March due to the economic impact of COVID-19. Companies like Consumer Portfolio Services and Santander Consumer USA experienced significant stock price declines, while Carvana fared better due to its online model and a substantial investment from Ally Financial. This downturn is largely attributed to concerns over rising delinquencies and charge-offs as customers face job losses and furloughs, stressing the subprime lending model.

title: U.S. Bank Net Income Drops 31 Percent
summary: U.S. Bank reported a 31 percent drop in net income to $1.2 billion in its first quarter, despite a 3.5 percent revenue increase to $5.8 billion. This decline reflects broader banking trends impacted by the Covid-19 economic meltdown, leading the bank to set aside nearly $1 billion for potential credit losses. U.S. Bank has also modified over $5.7 billion in loans and seen $22 billion in credit line drawdowns, while supporting employees and communities with wage increases and relief efforts.

title: Investors are cashing in from following the Fed this chart shows
summary: Investors are profiting by aligning their strategies with the Federal Reserve's actions, particularly its asset purchasing and emergency lending programs initiated during the coronavirus pandemic. This trend is evident in the narrowing yield spread between BBB-rated corporate bonds (lowest investment-grade) and BB-rated corporate bonds (highest non-investment-grade or "junk" bonds). This indicates that following the Fed's lead has been a successful strategy for investors.

title: Onex buys U.K.-based health care staffing company, weeks after CEO said market rife for acquisitions
summary: Onex Corp. has acquired Independent Clinical Services Group Ltd. (ICS), a U.K.-based health care staffing firm, capitalizing on opportunities CEO Gerry Schwartz identified during the pandemic. This acquisition marks the first major deal for a Canadian private-equity investor since the COVID-19 crisis began, with Onex leveraging its substantial cash reserves for the purchase. The deal highlights a trend of private-equity funds making strategic acquisitions amid market shifts.

title: ETF News, Trends, Analysis, Opinions
summary: Investors are shifting towards riskier, longer-duration products, moving further down the credit spectrum, indicating that the Federal Reserve's support measures have calmed markets. This shift is evidenced by significant outflows from short-dated bond ETFs and substantial inflows into corporate bond ETFs, with over $1.8 billion flowing into four such ETFs. The Fed's unprecedented decision to purchase corporate bonds as part of its quantitative easing, even expanding to recently downgraded credit, has reassured investors regarding the long-term economic impact of the coronavirus.

title: Santiago de Sousa es el nuevo CMO de BBVA Argentina
summary: Santiago de Sousa has been appointed as the new Chief Marketing Officer of BBVA Argentina, while also retaining his role as head of digital sales & UX/UI design. He replaces Santiago Sanguinetti, who moved to a brand strategy director position for Latin America at BBVA Creative. Additionally, Marcelo Parada is now the marketing strategy manager for BBVA Argentina.

title: Lawsuit alleges Wells Fargo unfairly shuffled Paycheck Protection Program applications
summary: A class-action lawsuit has been filed against Wells Fargo, alleging that the bank unfairly prioritized large loan applications for the government's Paycheck Protection Program (PPP), thus maximizing its processing fees. The lawsuit claims Wells Fargo reshuffled applications despite the program's first-come, first-served basis, potentially disadvantaging small businesses with fewer resources. This legal action comes after the $349 billion PPP fund, designed to help small businesses retain employees during the COVID-19 crisis, ran out of money.

title: Bank of Hawaii sets aside $33.6M for possible loan defaults amid coronavirus shutdown
summary: Bank of Hawaii reported a 40.9% drop in net income for the first quarter, setting aside $33.6 million for potential loan defaults due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The bank also suspended stock buybacks but declared a quarterly dividend of 67 cents a share. Despite the challenges, Bankoh processed numerous Paycheck Protection Program loans and made significant loan modifications, highlighting its strong financial position to support customers through the crisis.

title: Hedge Fund and Insider Trading News: Anthony Scaramucci, Pierre Andurand, Howard Marks, East Lodge Capital, Regeneron Pharmaceuticals Inc (REGN), Siebert Financial Corp. (SIEB), and More
summary: This article covers various news items related to hedge funds and insider trading, highlighting the struggles of East Lodge Capital, Anthony Scaramucci's refutation of severed ties with Citi, and Howard Marks' skeptical view on the stock market rally. It also discusses how fund managers are responding to COVID-19, the success of small hedge funds betting against shale, and Pierre Andurand's warnings about "crazy losses" in the oil market.

title: Banks Gave Richest Clients ‘Concierge Treatment’ for Pandemic Aid (Published 2020)
summary: During the initial rollout of the federal government's $349 billion Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) for small businesses, major banks like JPMorgan Chase, Citibank, and U.S. Bank prioritized applications from their wealthiest clients. These elite customers often received "concierge service," bypassing online portals and securing loans quickly, while many other small businesses struggled to even submit applications before funds ran out. This revealed a two-tiered system despite the program being advertised as first-come, first-served.

title: Phunware, a data firm for Trump campaign, got millions in coronavirus small business help
summary: Phunware, a digital technology company working for Donald Trump's re-election campaign, received a $2.85 million loan from the federal Paycheck Protection Program (PPP). This loan amount is significantly higher than the average PPP loan, raising questions amid a lawsuit alleging JPMorgan Chase favored larger clients. The company's unique capabilities in collecting smartphone location data and its ties to high-profile finance executives like Blythe Masters are highlighted.

title: JP Morgan AM restructures ETF sales team as Lake moves to the US
summary: JP Morgan Asset Management (JPMAM) has restructured its ETF sales team, adopting a regional model. Bryon Lake, previously head of international ETFs, has moved to the US as head of ETF distribution for Americas. Olivier Paquier will lead ETF distribution for EMEA, and Philippe El-Asmar will head distribution for Asia-Pacific, as the firm aims to accelerate the growth of its global ETF platform.

title: ETF People - Olivier Paquier
summary: This article profiles Olivier Paquier, the Global Head of ETF Sales at AXA IM. It details his extensive career history within the ETF industry, including roles at JP Morgan Asset Management, State Street, Amundi, and NYSE Euronext. The profile also highlights his educational background with degrees from Sorbonne University and Paris School of Business.

title: JPMorgan Chase names Tracy-Ann Lim as chief media officer
summary: JPMorgan Chase has promoted Tracy-Ann Lim to chief media officer, filling a role left vacant since 2019. Lim will oversee the company's brand safety efforts and overarching media strategy, reporting to chief marketing officer Leslie Gillin. She previously served as executive director, head of media, and has a background from various media agencies.

title: Chase approved to fund about $29 billion to 239,000 businesses through the Paycheck Protection Program
summary: JPMorgan Chase announced it has approved loans totaling approximately $29 billion to over 239,000 businesses through the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP), supporting 3 million employees. The firm emphasized that a significant portion of these loans went to small businesses, with an average loan amount of $123,000. JPMorgan Chase is also committed to not profiting from the PPP and has provided additional support to communities and small businesses through philanthropic efforts and financial services.

title: National Fuel to Acquire Shell’s Integrated Upstream and Midstream Assets in Pennsylvania
summary: National Fuel Gas Company announced its acquisition of Shell’s integrated upstream and midstream assets in Pennsylvania for approximately $541 million. This opportunistic acquisition is expected to be immediately accretive to free cash flow and earnings per share, enhancing National Fuel’s integrated strategy within Appalachia. The deal includes substantial natural gas reserves, production, and gathering infrastructure, generating significant synergies and improving operational efficiency.

title: 8 Investments to Protect Against an Inflation Spike
summary: This article identifies eight investment strategies to protect financial portfolios against inflation, ranging from real assets like real estate and commodities to financial instruments like Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) and growth-oriented stocks. It explains how different assets inherently maintain or increase value during inflationary periods and also advises on debt management by converting variable to fixed interest rates. The article concludes by emphasizing personal investment in skills and earnings potential as the most crucial defense against inflation.

title: Wells Fargo faces government investigations into its PPP loans
summary: Wells Fargo disclosed that federal and state authorities are investigating its lending practices under the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP). The bank, which had faced prior restrictions from the Federal Reserve due to past misconduct, initially limited its participation in the PPP before resuming loans after the Fed lifted its lending cap. Wells Fargo is the first major bank to announce an investigation into its PPP activities, amidst broader scrutiny of how the stimulus funds were distributed.

title: South African Rand to Hold April Ranges, Avoid New Lows Major Bank Says
summary: The South African Rand is expected to remain within its April trading ranges and avoid new lows, with global factors continuing to be the primary influence on its direction against the Dollar, according to Credit Suisse. Domestically, the Rand faced pressure from Eskom's R2.5bn loss due to reduced mining consumption, a R5.5bn government injection into South African Airways, and warnings of a potential 17% economic contraction. However, Credit Suisse believes domestic risks like political instability or a failure to secure international loans are unlikely enough to push the Rand significantly lower.

title: Jeffery Yabuki to step down as Fiserv CEO
summary: Jeffery Yabuki, CEO and chairman of Fiserv, Inc., will step down after 15 years, effective July 1, 2020. He will be succeeded by Frank Bisignano, currently Fiserv’s president, chief operating officer, and director. Yabuki will remain executive chairman for the remainder of 2020 to ensure a smooth transition.

title: Shell Divests Shale Gas Appalachia Assets to National Fuel
summary: National Fuel Gas Company (NFG) is acquiring Shell's upstream and midstream gathering assets in Pennsylvania for approximately $541 million, with an expected closing date of July 31, 2020. This acquisition will expand NFG's holdings in Tioga County, Pennsylvania, adding over 200,000 net acres and significant natural gas reserves and production, along with associated infrastructure. The deal is expected to be immediately accretive to NFG's earnings per share and generate substantial free cash flow, while Shell divests non-core assets to focus on higher-margin shale operations.

title: Citi Snags Barclays Equity Trading Chief After Year in Role
summary: Citigroup Inc. has hired Fater Belbachir from Barclays Plc to lead its global equities trading operation, less than a year after he joined Barclays in the same role. This move aims to boost Citi's standing in equities trading, an area where it has struggled with revenue and lagged behind competitors. Belbachir's departure follows a leadership shakeup at Barclays' investment bank last year.

title: TG Therapeutics Announces Proposed Public Offering of Common Stock | TGTX Stock News
summary: TG Therapeutics (TGTX) announced its intention to offer 6,000,000 shares of common stock in an underwritten public offering, with an option for underwriters to purchase an additional 15%. The proceeds are earmarked for the continued development of ublituximab and umbralisib, potential acquisitions, and general corporate purposes. J.P. Morgan, Jefferies, Evercore, and Cantor Fitzgerald are managing the offering.

title: JPMorgan Chase, American Homes 4 Rent plan to build thousands of single-family rental homes
summary: J.P. Morgan Asset Management and American Homes 4 Rent have formed a joint venture to build approximately 2,500 single-family rental homes in high-growth markets in the West and Southeast, deploying $625 million of equity. This initiative capitalizes on a trend of city dwellers seeking more space and suburban living, a shift accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic. The partnership has already begun construction, with the first homes expected to be delivered in June 2020 in Las Vegas.

title: Goldman Sachs eyes Wells Fargo, PNC, US Bancorp spiking stocks
summary: Speculation is rising that Goldman Sachs, under CEO David Solomon, may seek to acquire a major commercial bank like Wells Fargo, PNC, or U.S. Bancorp. This potential move would mark a significant shift for Goldman as it aims to boost its earnings amid squeezed profits from its trading business and declining fees in investment banking. The news caused a rally in financial stocks, with Wells Fargo, PNC, and U.S. Bancorp shares rising.

title: CoStar buying Ten-X Commercial to move commercial real estate deals online
summary: CoStar Group is acquiring Ten-X Commercial for $190 million to expand its online commercial real estate transaction capabilities. This acquisition aims to create an end-to-end platform by combining LoopNet and CoStar's buyer audience with Ten-X's online auction expertise, particularly in anticipation of a surge in distressed properties. This deal focuses solely on Ten-X Commercial, with private equity firm Thomas H. Lee Partners retaining ownership of Auction.com.

title: JP Morgan AM expands ETF team in Asia with BlackRock hire
summary: JP Morgan Asset Management (JPMAM) has appointed Rory Caines from BlackRock to its ETF team in Asia. Based in Hong Kong, Caines will focus on advancing the firm’s ETF product strategy for the APAC region and building client relationships, leveraging his prior experience in capital markets and fixed income ETFs at BlackRock. This hire aims to strengthen JPMAM's presence and product offerings for Asian investors.

title: Warren Buffett dumps Goldman Sachs holdings
summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Inc. significantly reduced its holdings in Goldman Sachs Group Inc. during the first quarter. This sale marks the winding down of an investment initiated during the 2008 financial crisis when Berkshire invested $5 billion to support the bank. The terms of this deal had been renegotiated five years after the initial investment.

title: 21 Stocks Warren Buffett Is Selling (And 1 He's Buying)
summary: During Q1 2020, Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway was a net seller of stocks, liquidating or trimming positions in 21 companies, most notably in the airline and banking sectors, while making only one significant purchase. This activity reflects a cautious stance amidst the economic uncertainty caused by the coronavirus pandemic, with many sales targeting long-held or smaller positions. The single purchase was an increase in its stake in PNC Financial Services, suggesting a specific conviction within the financial sector.

title: Galicia-Ualá: se consolida la colaboración entre la industria bancaria y las fintech
summary: The fintech Ualá has reached 2 million cards issued and is developing alliances with several financial entities, including Banco Galicia. Founder and CEO Pierpaolo Barbieri highlighted the collaborative model between banks and fintechs, emphasizing that Ualá's services are more affordable and aim for financial inclusion, especially outside major cities. The company has seen significant growth during the COVID-19 quarantine and plans to more than double its workforce by year-end.

title: This Jamie Dimon protege has weathered six crises. Here is his coronavirus playbook
summary: Frank Bisignano, the newly appointed CEO of Fiserv, shares his pandemic playbook, drawn from his experience navigating six past crises including 9/11 and the Great Recession. The article highlights his leadership strategies such as providing hazard pay for frontline workers, top executives taking pay cuts for a hardship fund, and maintaining investment in technology and employees by leveraging merger synergies. Bisignano's history of transforming struggling businesses and his unconventional thinking in financial services are also discussed.

title: Is Len Blavatnik about to complete the shrewdest deal in the history of the record business?
summary: The article discusses how Len Blavatnik's Access Industries is poised to entirely recover its $3.3 billion investment in Warner Music Group through dividends and the upcoming Nasdaq IPO, while still maintaining majority ownership. It highlights the potential for this to be one of the shrewdest deals in music business history, valuing WMG at approximately $16 billion post-IPO. Blavatnik is also set to retain significant voting power, effectively calling the shots.

title: Occidental is sued by shareholders, bondholders over Anadarko merger
summary: Occidental Petroleum is facing a lawsuit from shareholders and bondholders who claim they incurred billions in losses due to the company's alleged concealment of its financial vulnerability after acquiring Anadarko Petroleum for $35.7 billion. Investors argue that Occidental failed to disclose in its registration statements how quadrupling its debt would expose it to falling oil prices and undermine its ability to maintain its dividend and boost shale oil production. The lawsuit also names Occidental's CEO, former CFO, several directors, and banks that underwrote its bonds, alleging inadequate due diligence.

title: Golden Bulls: Visualizing the Price of Gold from 1915-2020
summary: This article visualizes the price of gold from 1915 to 2020, identifying three "Golden Bulls" or periods of exceptional performance since 1969. It delves into the history of the gold standard in the U.S., government interventions, and the economic conditions that drove gold's price during each bull market. The analysis highlights gold's long-term value as a financial asset amidst various economic upheavals, including inflation, financial crises, and political uncertainty.

title: Christine Y. Zhao Celebrated for Dedication to the Field of Finance
summary: Christine Y. Zhao has been recognized by Marquis Who's Who for her extensive and accomplished career in finance, spanning more than two decades. She currently serves as a Board Director for Nasdaq-listed BeyondSpring Inc. and a Venture Partner at YuanMing Capital, having previously held significant roles at JPMorgan, Bank of America Merrill Lynch, and as CFO for private equity-backed companies including Best Inc. Her career highlights include driving strategy, business execution, and successful financial initiatives across various global institutions and industries, in addition to her significant community involvement.

title: PNC Appoints Chief Investment Officer for PNC Bank, N.A.
summary: PNC Financial Services Group, Inc. announced the appointment of Gagan Singh as senior vice president and managing director of asset and liability management for the corporation and chief investment officer for PNC Bank, National Association. Singh will be responsible for oversight and management of PNC's portfolio and proprietary trading, reporting to E. William Parsley. His extensive experience in interest rate derivatives and mortgage-backed securities is expected to maximize shareholder value.

title: Chinese Gaming Firm NetEase to Launch $2.5 Billion Hong Kong Stock Sale
summary: Chinese game developer NetEase Inc. is preparing to launch a $2.5 billion stock offering in Hong Kong, following a trend of U.S.-listed Chinese companies seeking secondary listings in the city amid rising U.S.-China tensions. This move, along with JD.com Inc.'s planned $3 billion offering, highlights a shift towards Hong Kong as a listing destination, especially after a proposed U.S. bill could force Chinese companies to delist from American markets. NetEase plans to use the proceeds for expansion into music streaming and online education, with its Hong Kong debut expected on June 11.

title: Wells Fargo Corporate Risk Announces Enhanced Organizational Structure and New Leaders
summary: Wells Fargo & Company announced an enhanced organizational structure for its Corporate Risk division and the appointment of two new leaders, Kevin Reen and Bill Juliano. This new model includes five line-of-business Chief Risk Officers reporting to Wells Fargo CRO Mandy Norton, alongside other teams aligned by risk type, to strengthen risk management and provide greater oversight. The changes aim to further transform risk management practices and better position the company for the future.

title: Capital One Announces Capital One, National Association and Capital One Bank (USA), National Association Any and All Cash Tender Offers for $7.55 Billion of Notes
summary: Capital One announced cash tender offers for approximately $7.55 billion of notes issued by its subsidiaries, Capital One, National Association, and Capital One Bank (USA), National Association. The offers allow holders to sell certain securities back to Capital One for cash, with varying purchase prices depending on the note series. The tender offers are set to expire on June 5, 2020, with a settlement date expected on June 10, 2020.

title: Western Union makes offer to buy MoneyGram
summary: Western Union Co. is reportedly seeking to acquire rival money transfer company MoneyGram International Inc. A takeover offer has been made, though no final decision has been reached. This potential merger would bring together two major U.S. money transfer service providers in a declining market.

title: Warner Music Group Corp. Announces Pricing of Initial Public Offering
summary: Warner Music Group Corp. announced the pricing of its initial public offering (IPO) of 77,000,000 shares of Class A common stock at $25.00 per share, an increase from the previously announced 70,000,000 shares. The offering consists entirely of secondary shares sold by Access Industries, LLC and related selling stockholders, with the company not receiving any proceeds. Shares are expected to begin trading on Nasdaq under the ticker "WMG" on June 3, 2020.

title: Citigroup forms new strategic advisory group to merge insights, data
summary: Citigroup Inc. has announced the formation of a new strategic advisory group within its investment bank, led by Muir Paterson. This group, combining financial strategy and data science capabilities, aims to offer broader client insights into asset bases, corporate finance, and tax strategies. The initiative comes as companies face potential proxy battles, and rivals like Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan have also moved to integrate shareholder defense with data science.

title: No quiet retirement for longtime Webster Financial chief
summary: James Smith, former CEO of Webster Financial, is actively involved in developing an economic action plan for Connecticut, even in retirement, demonstrating a continued commitment to public service. His work, initially derailed by COVID-19, now focuses on reopening, recovery, and reimagining the state's economy, with a particular concern for small businesses and urban centers. Smith advocates for retired bankers to invest their career knowledge back into their communities, emphasizing the noble nature of banking and civic responsibility.

title: Flexion Therapeutics Raises $90MM in a Tough Market
summary: Flexion Therapeutics successfully raised $90 million through a public offering, exceeding initial expectations despite a challenging market. The biopharmaceutical company, which focuses on musculoskeletal conditions, plans to use the funds to advance its product pipeline, including additional indications for Zilretta and development of FX201. Goldman Sachs & Co, LLC. and Credit Suisse served as joint book-running managers for the offering.

title: Five fund buyers highlight areas for fixed income ETF innovation
summary: Five fund buyers discuss the need for innovation in the European fixed income ETF market, which is currently dominated by broad-based ETFs. Key areas for development include greater granularity, improved currency hedging at lower costs, credit ETFs segmented by maturity, and the creation of fundamental and ESG-rated indices. The article emphasizes the potential for significant growth in this market over the next five years.

title: Morgan Stanley's Gorman 'thrilled' with ETrade purchase
summary: Morgan Stanley CEO James Gorman expresses immense satisfaction with the acquisition of ETrade, highlighting the online trading firm's technology, digital banking capabilities, and management team. He plans to retain the ETrade brand, possibly as "ETrade powered by Morgan Stanley," recognizing its value to clients. Gorman believes the deal expands Morgan Stanley's online platform, diversifies the company, and strengthens its digital offerings, particularly appealing to a younger demographic.

title: Tiger Trade Launches SGX Trading, to Meet Increased Demand from Singapore and Southeast Asian Investors
summary: Tiger Trade, a mobile and online trading application by Tiger Brokers, has launched access to the Singapore Exchange (SGX) to cater to increased demand from Singapore and Southeast Asian investors. This expansion adds to their existing offerings of major global stock exchanges and allows users to invest in a wider range of financial instruments. The move comes as Tiger Trade observed a significant surge in trading volumes and new accounts opened among Singapore-based retail investors during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Hedge Fund and Insider Trading News: Kyle Bass, Davidson Kempner Capital Management, BirchLane Capital, Bodenholm Capital, Brahman Capital, Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp (AQN), Flexsteel Industries, Inc. (FLXS), and More
summary: This article compiles various hedge fund and insider trading news items. Key stories include Davidson Kempner acquiring Oak Furnitureland, BirchLane Capital starting with $200 million, Bill Ackman divesting his stake in Berkshire Hathaway, and the SEC investigating Kyle Bass's statements regarding UDF. Additionally, news on Brahman Capital launching an ESG fund and hedge funds experiencing losses on Greek and Italian shorts are covered.

title: JPMorgan Chase to close branches early on Friday in observation of Juneteenth
summary: JPMorgan Chase announced it will close its U.S. Chase retail branches early on Friday, June 19, in observance of Juneteenth. CEO Jamie Dimon stated this decision reflects respect for the Black community and allows employees time to reflect and participate in events. This move follows several other major companies recognizing Juneteenth as a holiday amid nationwide protests against racial injustice.

title: American Express And Chase Utterly Fail To Protect Me From Crooked Merchant (Dispute Horror Story)
summary: The author recounts a "horror story" involving a six-figure dispute with an Italian merchant for damaged designer handbags, where both American Express and Chase sided with the merchant despite strong contractual evidence. The article highlights the failure of credit card companies to protect consumers and small businesses in large B2B transactions, prompting the author to share warnings and seek legal redress.

title: Hester Serafini Appointed President of ICE Clear Europe
summary: Intercontinental Exchange, Inc. (ICE) has appointed Hester Serafini as President of ICE Clear Europe, its London-based clearing house. Serafini, who previously served as Interim President, was selected for her extensive experience within ICE and global finance, having also been President and COO of ICE Clear U.S. Kevin McClear has been appointed as her successor at ICE Clear U.S.

title: The 20-Year Bond Is Changing The Shape Of The Yield Curve
summary: The U.S. Treasury's re-issuance of 20-year bonds in May 2020, for the first time since 1986, is significantly altering the shape of the yield curve. This new issuance has created a "kink" in the curve, with front-end rates indicating lower interest rates while longer-dated rates have moved higher. As liquidity in this sector builds, experts anticipate that the kink will moderate, influencing futures trading and overall market liquidity.

title: Juneteenth emerges as company holiday as Nike, Citigroup and others commemorate black history
summary: An increasing number of U.S. companies, including Nike, Citigroup, Twitter, and Uber, are recognizing Juneteenth as a paid company holiday to commemorate the liberation of slaves after the Civil War. This move follows the death of George Floyd and a growing call for racial justice, with experts suggesting observing Juneteenth can improve perception among black workers and consumers. While it presents a risk of becoming just another day off, companies are encouraged to use the day to learn about their historical connections to slavery.

title: Carlyle to invest $415 mn in KB Financial, betting on share rebound
summary: Carlyle Group plans to invest $415 million in KB Financial Group through exchangeable bonds and additional injections, aiming to become a significant shareholder. This investment, marking Carlyle's first equity deal in a South Korean financial firm in two decades, includes a strategic alliance to enhance global and domestic investment activities for both companies. The move is based on Carlyle's expectation of a rebound in KB shares, despite recent underperformance.

title: Banking by appointment could stick as a post-COVID-19 customer habit
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has led financial institutions to implement appointment-based banking to manage social distancing, a practice that some bankers believe will continue post-pandemic. This system helps banks manage staff levels, triage customers, and offer convenience for customers working from home. It also complements digital banking options for those who still prefer a personal touch, with banks like Regions seeing a significant increase in appointment volume.

title: Brazilian Brokerage XP Shares Surge, Landing Its Chairman A $3 Billion Fortune
summary: Guilherme Benchimol, chairman of Brazilian brokerage XP Inc, has seen his net worth surge to $3 billion due to a rise in XP stock, making him one of Brazil's richest individuals. Benchimol co-founded XP Investimentos in 2001, which has since grown into one of Brazil's largest brokerage firms. Despite fierce competition and market volatility, XP continues to expand, recently acquiring an online insurance marketplace.

title: PFPC Selected by Franklin Templeton Investments to Service New Jersey 529 Plans
summary: PFPC Inc., a member of The PNC Financial Services Group, Inc., has been selected by Franklin Templeton Investments to provide investor servicing for both the Franklin Templeton 529 College Savings Plan and the NJBEST 529 College Savings Plan. This multi-year contract involves PFPC providing recordkeeping, reporting, and investor servicing for these plans, expanding its role in the growing 529 college savings plan market. The collaboration will leverage PFPC's Global Enterprise Platform to support expanded distribution goals and complex servicing needs for these college savings programs.

title: J.P. Morgan Argentina | About us
summary: J.P. Morgan has a long-standing commitment to Argentina, operating there for over 125 years and playing a significant role in the country's financial landscape. The firm provides a range of services from its Buenos Aires office, combining specialist knowledge with market leadership, and is dedicated to community development and education through philanthropic efforts. Facundo Gómez Minujín, CEO for Argentina, Uruguay, Bolivia, and Paraguay, emphasizes the bank's continuous presence and growth plans, including the Buenos Aires Corporate Center (BACC) which employs around 3,000 people.

title: Japan's SoftBank unloads a $21 billion stake in T-Mobile US as the great sell-off commences
summary: SoftBank Group Corp. is selling a $21 billion stake in T-Mobile US Inc. as part of a larger $42 billion asset sale to finance stock buybacks and reduce debt, motivated by record losses in its Vision Fund. This move comes after significant write-downs in investments like WeWork and Uber. The complex transaction involves T-Mobile holding a public offering and transferring nearly 200 million shares owned by SoftBank.

title: CoreLogic Weighs Unsolicited Bid from Cannae Holdings, Senator Investment Group
summary: Cannae Holdings Inc. and Senator Investment Group LP have proposed acquiring CoreLogic Inc. for $5.16 billion, or $65 a share in cash, representing a 37% premium over CoreLogic's stock price on June 15. CoreLogic stated it would review the unsolicited bid, with the bidders criticizing CoreLogic's current strategy and recent guidance change as a defensive move. The firms are calling for CoreLogic to hire advisers and form a special committee to negotiate the transaction.

title: Nelnet And Great Lakes Will No Longer Service Your Federal Student Loans
summary: Nelnet and Great Lakes, which service federal student loans for approximately 13 million borrowers, may no longer service federal student loans after December 2020. This decision by the U.S. Department of Education, led by Betsy DeVos, aims to improve student loan servicing through new contracts with five other servicers. Borrowers are advised to continue making payments to Nelnet or Great Lakes until a new servicer is assigned and to update auto-payments accordingly.

title: Netflix will move $100 million into Black-owned banks
summary: Netflix Inc. is pledging $100 million to Black-owned banks and financial institutions to support African-American communities. This initiative involves an initial $25 million investment in the Black Economic Development Initiative and $10 million to Hope Credit Union, with an ongoing commitment to steer 2% of its cash to these organizations. This move follows calls for corporate support for racial equality and aims to address systemic inequality by boosting historically underfunded institutions.

title: Cetera Hires Ex-Stifel Recruiting Head John Pierce
summary: John R. Pierce, formerly a senior recruiter at Ameriprise Financial Services and Stifel, Nicolaus, has been appointed Head of Business Development at Cetera Financial Group. Pierce, who previously oversaw recruiting for Ameriprise's employee channel and then spent four years at Stifel, will report to Tim Stinson, Cetera’s head of wealth management and recruiting. His hire comes as Cetera, controlled by private equity firm Genstar, faces financial scrutiny with Moody's cutting its credit outlook for parent company Aretec Group to negative from stable due to high fixed-rate debt and sensitivity to revenue declines.

title: First look: JPMorgan Chase's downtown branch to open next week
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. is opening its newest Nashville branch next week at the base of the ServiceSource Tower in downtown Nashville. This will be the bank's flagship Nashville location, situated near Broadway and several competitors like Regions Bank, Fifth Third Bank, and SunTrust Bank.

title: J2 Global: Troubling Related Party Transactions, Looming Impairments And A Suspicious History Of Insider Enrichment Spanning Decades
summary: Hindenburg Research exposes J2 Global's alleged history of insider self-enrichment, related-party transactions, and questionable accounting practices. The report details how J2's opaque acquisition system, led by its VP of Corporate Development, may have facilitated millions in insider gains, while key business metrics decline and significant impairments remain undisclosed at the parent company level despite being recorded by subsidiaries. The article also highlights severe corporate governance issues, including conflicted independent board members and the CEO's exorbitant compensation.

title: U.S. offshore RMB accounts open the door to growth opportunities in China
summary: China has made significant efforts to open its markets to foreign companies, presenting growth opportunities for financial institutions and international investors. J.P. Morgan, as the first non-Chinese offshore RMB clearing bank in the U.S. approved by the People’s Bank of China, supports financial institutions with cross-border RMB payment needs. This capability allows U.S. financial institutions to offer their clients more effective ways to transact with Chinese trading partners and navigate the complex payments landscape in China.

title: BBVA brings ‘banker bar’ to new branches in Texas expansion
summary: BBVA USA is expanding its presence in Texas by opening 15 new branches, despite the coronavirus pandemic. These new branches will feature a "personal banker bar" instead of traditional tellers, aiming to merge digital and physical banking experiences. The bank plans to retrain existing tellers and new employees to facilitate digital onboarding and account origination, with a goal to complete this re-skilling by 2021.

title: BBVA Banking as a service investment solarisBank announces significant new funding to accelerate its growth
summary: solarisBank, a German technology company with a banking license and a BBVA investment, has secured a new €60 million Series C funding round. This oversubscribed funding, with BBVA's participation, will accelerate solarisBank's growth, expand its Banking-as-a-Service market leadership in Europe, and strengthen its regulatory capital. The company, founded in 2016, enables over 80 companies to offer compliant financial services and has doubled its revenues yearly since 2017.

title: JP Morgan Chase creates financial pathways for Black college graduates
summary: JPMorgan Chase launched the Advancing Black Pathways Career Readiness Series, an online program for recent graduates of historically Black colleges and young professionals of color. The program aims to uplift young African Americans by providing financial literacy, career advice, and interview skills, especially in a virtual environment. JPMorgan Chase has committed to hiring 4,000 Black college graduates by 2024 through initiatives like this, addressing the challenges faced by new graduates during economic uncertainty.

title: Waterstone Mortgage Head Andy Peach To Resign
summary: Andy Peach, President and CEO of Waterstone Mortgage Corporation, has announced his resignation. Peach, who was appointed last August, is leaving the role with over 30 years of industry experience. A replacement has not yet been named.

title: USDA Rural Dev.’t awards 5 Puerto Rico banks for $109M in lending
summary: The U.S. Department of Agriculture Rural Development office in Puerto Rico recognized five local banks with "Top Lenders Awards" for collectively approving $109 million in home loans. This initiative celebrates "Homeownership Month" and highlights the partnership between USDA Rural and local lenders, which has helped over 3,700 families purchase homes in 2020. Despite challenges, USDA Rural Development has invested nearly $447 million in Puerto Rico for homeownership and provided additional funds for home repairs and housing preservation grants.

title: Annexon grabs $100M from a host of top VC firms for complement therapies
summary: Annexon Biosciences has successfully closed a $100 million financing round, attracting a prominent group of new and existing VC investors. The funding will be used to advance its clinical pipeline, including ANX005 for Guillain-Barré syndrome and other conditions, and ANX007 for complement-mediated neurodegenerative ophthalmic disorders. The company aims to accelerate its clinical and preclinical programs to address autoimmune and neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Credicorp emite bonos por 500 millones de dólares en el mercado internacional
summary: Credicorp, a Peruvian financial services holding company, issued $500 million in bonds in international markets with a coupon rate of 2.750% and maturity in 2025. The proceeds from this operation will be used to finance corporate purposes. Various law firms advised Credicorp and the initial purchasers, Bank of America Securities, J.P. Morgan Securities, and Goldman Sachs.

title: Even popular Ford F-Series hit hard amid plummeting industry sales
summary: Despite the Ford F-Series helping Ford Motor Co. achieve the smallest second-quarter sales drop among the Detroit Three, the popular pickup still experienced a significant decline in sales. The article details the sales performance of Ford, General Motors, and Fiat Chrysler Automobiles during a challenging second quarter due to the coronavirus pandemic, noting that while overall sales were down, the average transaction prices for vehicles increased. Analysts weigh in on Ford's performance, highlighting bright spots like the Explorer and Ranger, and discuss the uncertain market outlook for the next quarter.

title: Exclusive: JPMorgan drops terms 'master,' 'slave' from internal tech code and materials
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co is removing terms like "blacklist," "master," and "slave" from its internal technology code and materials to address racism within the company, following similar moves by other tech firms. This significant investment highlights the financial sector's re-examination of racially problematic language, a change that could be costly and complex given the intertwined nature of banking technology.

title: Valley National Bank views today's business environment as a glass half full
summary: Valley National Bank's Tampa-based commercial real estate lending team is cautiously optimistic about the region's economic rebound despite the COVID-19 pandemic. They are implementing stricter lending practices, including requiring more equity and increased due diligence, but have also processed over $2.3 billion in PPP loans. The bank is buoyed by falling unemployment claims, rising consumer confidence, and anticipates growth in certain commercial real estate sectors.

title: Exclusive: JPMorgan drops terms 'master,' 'slave' from internal tech code and materials
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. is removing terms like "blacklist," "master," and "slave" from its internal technology code and materials in an effort to address racism within the company. This move follows similar changes by technology companies like Twitter and GitHub, prompted by renewed discussions about racial equality after the death of George Floyd. While changing these entrenched terms in complex banking systems could be costly and time-consuming, it signifies a significant investment by JPMorgan in promoting an anti-bias culture.

title: Banks Could Get $24 Billion in Fees From PPP Loans
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Bank of America Corp. are projected to earn between $1.5 billion and $2.6 billion in fees from the government's Paycheck Protection Program (PPP), acting as leading conduits for small-business aid during the coronavirus shutdown. The two largest banks by assets processed more emergency loans than other lenders and are poised to receive the largest fees, according to recent disclosures by the Trump administration.

title: Chicago Quantum Exchange announces seven new partnerships to advance research, training
summary: The Chicago Quantum Exchange (CQE), a research hub based at the University of Chicago, has announced seven new corporate partnerships to advance quantum technology research and development. These new partners include Intel, JPMorgan Chase, Microsoft, Quantum Design, Qubitekk, Rigetti Computing, and Zurich Instruments, expanding CQE's collaborations to a total of 13 companies. The partnerships aim to accelerate discovery, develop quantum applications, and prepare a skilled quantum workforce by leveraging expertise from universities, national laboratories, and industry leaders.

title: BBVA is the first financial institution in the world to issue green CoCo bonds
summary: BBVA has become the first financial institution globally to issue a green contingent convertible (CoCo) bond, raising €1 billion. The bond was nearly thrice oversubscribed and attracted significant investor interest, particularly from those with ESG criteria, allowing BBVA to lower the yield. This issuance aligns with BBVA's strategic focus on sustainable finance and contributes to its pledge to mobilize €100 billion by 2025.

title: IVA IPO News - French NASH biotech Inventiva increases range ahead of $108 million US IPO
summary: Inventiva, a French biotech company specializing in NASH therapies, has increased the proposed price range for its upcoming US IPO to raise $108 million. The company plans to offer 7.5 million ADSs at $13.40 to $15.40 each, expecting to raise 5% more in proceeds than initially projected. Inventiva's lead candidate, lanifibranor, is in Phase 2b trials for NASH, with positive results already announced.

title: Increase in Global Liquidity May Help Equities and Bonds, Says JPMorgan
summary: JPMorgan strategists forecast a significant increase in global debt, reaching $200 trillion by year-end, which will be coupled with increased liquidity. This surge in cash, driven by higher savings rates and accommodative central bank policies, is expected to fuel asset reflation and eventually flow into equities and bonds, supporting their performance. Investors are encouraged to consider building portfolios with optimal equity and bond allocations, potentially using ETFs like GSEW and GIGB.

title: Deutsche Bank eagerly took on clients dumped by JP Morgan Chase. Now it's facing big fines
summary: Deutsche Bank is facing substantial fines for continuing to do business with clients that JPMorgan Chase had previously dropped due to compliance concerns, including convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and banks Danske Bank A/S and FBME Bank Ltd. The New York Department of Financial Services levied $150 million in penalties against Deutsche Bank for missing or disregarding compliance red flags over several years. This situation arose after JPMorgan offloaded these high-risk clients to improve its anti-money laundering controls following regulatory warnings in 2013.

title: Rocky Mountain Institute launches the Center for Climate-Aligned Finance
summary: Rocky Mountain Institute (RMI) has launched the Center for Climate-Aligned Finance in collaboration with major financial institutions like Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, Bank of America, and JPMorgan Chase. The Center aims to facilitate the financial sector's role in guiding the global economy to net-zero emissions by mid-century by developing practical solutions and frameworks for carbon-intensive industries. It will work with financial institutions and corporations to accelerate the transition to a sustainable energy platform and foster climate alignment initiatives across various sectors.

title: PPP in CNY: Top 20 banks, lenders that doled out most loans to local businesses
summary: This article identifies the top 20 banks and lenders that distributed the most Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loans to local businesses in Central New York. It highlights that independent community banks and credit unions performed the majority of lending, with M&T Bank leading. The article also provides a list of the top lenders and details about loan size distribution.

title: ING Groep to Shut Branches Amid Shift Toward Digitalization
summary: ING Groep announced plans to close 42 branches in the Netherlands due to a decline in foot traffic, accelerated by the coronavirus pandemic and a broader shift towards digital banking. The bank, led by CEO Ruud van Dusschoten, intends to transfer services to existing service points and offer affected employees other positions within the company. This move aligns with ING's long-term strategy of focusing on digital capabilities, a trend also seen in other major banks.

title: Golpeado por la pandemia, IRSA sale a buscar fondos para refinanciar deuda
summary: IRSA Inversiones y Representaciones, heavily impacted by the economic effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, is seeking to raise up to $300 million in fresh funds from capital markets to refinance its debt. The real estate holding company, led by Eduardo Elsztain, faces significant foreign currency debt maturities of $450 million between July and November this year. Rating agencies like S&P have warned about the risks IRSA faces due to its exposure to Argentina's economic conditions and the uncertainty generated by the coronavirus on its businesses, particularly its shopping centers, hotels, and offices.

title: HP Enterprise to buy Silver Peak for about $925 million
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co announced its intention to acquire Silver Peak, a developer of wide area network (WAN) performance tools, for approximately $925 million in cash. This acquisition aims to bolster HPE's software-defined wide-area network (SD-WAN) capabilities, integrating Silver Peak into its Aruba business unit. The move is particularly relevant given the increased demand for remote work solutions due to the COVID-19 pandemic, with HPE anticipating significant growth in the SD-WAN market.

title: Despite a massive recession, JPMorgan Chase just posted record revenue — here's how the bank did it
summary: JPMorgan Chase achieved record quarterly revenue of $33.8 billion in Q2 2020 despite a recession, largely thanks to its investment bank, which posted a record $5.5 billion profit. Shrewd moves made under CEO Jamie Dimon to build up the investment bank after the financial crisis, combined with surging market volatility and Federal Reserve actions, created an excellent environment for trading and advisory services. This strong performance in its Wall Street division helped offset significant losses in the bank's consumer and commercial banking segments, which were impacted by loan default provisions related to the pandemic.

title: BBVA, the best bank in Latin America according to Euromoney
summary: Euromoney magazine has named BBVA the best bank in Latin America for 2020, also recognizing it as the best in sustainable finance for the second consecutive year. The publication highlighted BBVA's successful integration of digitization across the region and its strong financial performance, with Latin American operations contributing significantly to the group's overall results. Additionally, BBVA was named the best bank in Mexico and Argentina, lauded for its digital transformation efforts, efficiency, customer satisfaction, and commitment to sustainable development.

title: Goldman Traders’ Best Result in Years Spurs Surprise Profit Gain
summary: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. saw a surprise profit gain in the second quarter, driven by a 93% surge in revenue from trading stocks and bonds. This performance, significantly exceeding analyst expectations, comes as the bank also achieved record underwriting fees amid a historic market rebound and Federal Reserve stimulus efforts. CEO David Solomon noted that recent market turbulence reinforced the bank's commitment to its strategy.

title: Morgan Stanley beats estimates for second-quarter profit on strong trading results
summary: Morgan Stanley reported its second-quarter 2020 earnings, significantly surpassing analysts' estimates due to robust trading results. The bank achieved a record profit of $3.2 billion, or $1.96 a share, and revenue climbed 30% to a record $13.4 billion, driven by strong performances in fixed income and equities trading, as well as wealth management. CEO James Gorman highlighted the success of the bank's business transformation in providing stability during stressful times and indicated potential future dividend increases and share buybacks.

title: Freeport freezes workers’ pensions
summary: Freeport-McMoRan Inc. announced it would freeze employee pension plans, ceasing all benefit accruals as of September 1, 2020, though existing benefits remain protected. This move has sparked speculation that the company might be up for sale, with past rumors involving Barrick Gold and Newmont Corporation. An financial advisor from Ash Creek Financial Advisors provided advice for employees on managing their retirement plans in light of these changes.

title: Berkeley Lights Announces Pricing of Initial Public Offering
summary: Berkeley Lights, Inc. announced the pricing of its initial public offering of 8,100,000 shares of common stock at $22.00 per share, expecting to raise approximately $178.2 million. The company's common stock is set to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol "BLI" on July 17, 2020. J.P. Morgan, Morgan Stanley, and Cowen are serving as lead book-running managers for the offering.

title: Wilson Sonsini Advises Ascentage Pharma in HK$702 Million Placing
summary: Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati advised Ascentage Pharma Group International in a private placement that raised HK$702 million. The biotechnology company, focused on novel therapies for cancers, HBV, and age-related diseases, placed 15,000,000 shares at HK$46.80 per share through Citi and J.P. Morgan. The Wilson Sonsini team was led by partner Wanda Woo.

title: Kidney diagnostics developer Renalytix AI prices US IPO at $13.50
summary: Renalytix AI, a developer of AI-powered diagnostic tests for kidney disease, priced its US IPO at $13.50 per ADS equivalent, raising $74 million. The company will list on the Nasdaq under the symbol RNLX. J.P. Morgan and Stifel were the lead managers for the offering.

title: Indigenous Resistance Expels Oil Company GeoPark from Peruvian Amazon
summary: The oil company GeoPark (NYSE:GPRK) announced its departure from Block 64 in the Peruvian Amazon following years of fierce opposition from the Achuar People of the Pastaza and the Wampis Nation. This withdrawal is a result of sustained indigenous resistance, involving protests, lawsuits, and advocacy campaigns targeting investors and the company's CEO. Indigenous leaders and Amazon Watch emphasized this as a victory for territorial rights and a call for investors to divest from destructive resource extraction in the Amazon.

title: FD interest rate revised by ICICI Bank! Compare latest rates with SBI, HDFC Bank – July 2020
summary: ICICI Bank has revised its fixed deposit (FD) interest rates downwards, effective July 14, making it the only leading bank to do so in July. This article compares the latest FD rates of ICICI Bank with those of SBI and HDFC Bank, highlighting that HDFC Bank offers the highest interest on 1-year FDs, while ICICI Bank leads for longer tenures (5-10 years). Both ICICI Bank and SBI have special "Golden Years" or "Wecare" FD schemes offering additional benefits for senior citizens for a limited period.

title: KB Kookmin to own 67% of Indonesia's Bank Bukopin
summary: KB Kookmin Bank announced its plan to become the largest shareholder of Indonesia's Bank Bukopin, aiming for a 67% stake by the end of August. This acquisition, approved on July 16, will be one of the lowest-priced Indonesian bank purchases in the last five years. KB Kookmin Bank plans to enhance Bank Bukopin's risk-management and digital finance capabilities.

title: SEC charges former Morgan Stanley rep with stealing $6 million from clients
summary: The SEC has charged Michael Barry Carter, a former Morgan Stanley representative, with stealing approximately $6 million from brokerage customers and an elderly investment advisory client through unauthorized transfers between 2007 and 2019. Carter has pleaded guilty to parallel criminal charges and was fired by Morgan Stanley in 2019, with the firm stating that impacted clients have been reimbursed. He used the misappropriated funds to support a lavish lifestyle and concealed the fraud with false account statements.

title: Wells Fargo Names Mike Santomassimo as New Chief Financial Officer
summary: Wells Fargo & Company announced that Mike Santomassimo will join the company in fall 2020 as Chief Financial Officer, succeeding John Shrewsberry. Santomassimo previously served as CFO at BNY Mellon and held key finance leadership roles at JPMorgan Chase. John Shrewsberry will retire after a 22-year career with Wells Fargo, including six years as CFO, and will assist with the transition.

title: What BlackRock's continued dominance means for other ETF issuers
summary: BlackRock continues its dominance in the ETF market, fueled by increased interest in its fixed-income and cash management services and strategic fee cuts. While BlackRock and Vanguard account for a significant portion of ETF assets, smaller firms like Ark Invest are growing rapidly by offering specialized, actively managed funds. This creates a dual market where investors rely on large firms for passive index products and on niche players for alpha generation and diversification.

title: More Wells Fargo customers say the bank decided to pause their mortgage payments without asking
summary: Numerous Wells Fargo customers across 14 states claim the bank unilaterally placed their mortgages into forbearance plans, affecting their credit reports and ability to refinance, without their consent. The bank attributes these incidents to misinterpretations of customer intentions, while critics like Sen. Sherrod Brown denounce the bank's "sloppy service and shoddy management." This practice has drawn comparisons to Wells Fargo's past scandals of enrolling customers in unwanted services.

title: Morgan Stanley is starting to come clean about climate change
summary: Morgan Stanley is the first U.S.-based global bank to join the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF), an international collaboration aimed at standardizing carbon accounting for the financial sector. This move signifies a commitment from the finance giant to disclose how its investments and loans contribute to climate change, following increasing pressure from climate activist groups and previous steps towards more environmentally friendly investments. The bank has financed over $91 billion in fossil fuel ventures since 2016, highlighting the significance of its new commitment to transparency.

title: BTG Pactual obtém 514,1 milhões de dólares em emissão de unidades locais e internacionais
summary: BTG Pactual successfully raised $514.1 million through a primary public offering of 35,625,000 units, with each unit equivalent to one common share and two Class A preferred shares. The funds will be allocated to strategic initiatives within its digital retail business and to bolster its capital indicators.
