Banks should consider five strategic actions: reviewing processes, targeting differentiation, developing talent, aligning product offerings with client needs, and focusing on client experience.

title: West Virginia bars JPMorgan, Wells, Goldman from new state contracts
summary: West Virginia has barred JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and BlackRock from new state contracts, citing their policies to reduce financing for coal companies. This action follows a new state law allowing West Virginia's treasurer, Riley Moore, to restrict financial institutions that "boycott" fossil fuels. While U.S. Bank avoided the ban by eliminating anti-coal policies, the other institutions disputed the boycott notion, with JPMorgan calling the decision "shortsighted."

title: Is this the easiest way to attract new clients?
summary: JPMorgan Chase has introduced "Chase MyHome," a virtual platform designed to simplify the homebuying process for potential homeowners, allowing them to search properties, apply for mortgages, and review financial details digitally. This initiative, along with similar efforts from companies like Welcome Homes, reflects a growing trend in the housing market to leverage technology to attract clients and streamline complex processes, especially in the wake of increased digital adoption during the pandemic. Chase MyHome has already proven successful, with 31% of home lending leads in early 2022 originating from customers who used the platform.

title: Have We Reached an Inflection Point for Global Bonds?
summary: The global bond market experienced a dismal first half of the year, with significant declines in major treasury indexes due to inflation, interest rate hikes, and global monetary tightening. However, recent central bank activity, including rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve and the ECB, suggests a potential turning point for global sovereign debt performance. Investors are now seeking safety, leading to a rally in global bond indexes and a retreat in yields, with all eyes on the US Fed's next moves.

title: Should You Pounce on These 8%-Yielding Preferreds?
summary: This article discusses preferred stocks as a hybrid investment offering high, stable yields, particularly through closed-end funds (CEFs). It highlights three specific CEFs—Cohen & Steers Tax-Advantaged Preferred Securities and Income Fund (PTA), Flaherty & Crumrine Preferred and Income Securities Fund (FFC), and Nuveen Preferred & Income Opportunities (JPC)—that offer over 8% dividends. The author advises caution due to current market conditions but recommends adding these funds to a watchlist for their income-generating potential.

title: Financing Secured for 85 Cleaveland Road, Pleasant Hill, Contra Costa County
summary: Construction financing totaling $94.3 million has been secured for a 189-unit residential development at 85 Cleaveland Road in Pleasant Hill, Contra Costa County. The project, arranged by JLL Capital Markets, involves Gemdale USA, Bank OZK, and AvalonBay Communities. Designed by KTGY Architecture + Planning, the development will include 19 low-income housing units and offers resort-style amenities, with construction expected to take 24 months.

title: Charles Schwab's $655B Asset Management Arm to Start Trading Crypto-Related ETF This Week
summary: Charles Schwab's asset management arm, Schwab Asset Management, which manages $655 billion, is set to offer its first crypto-related exchange-traded fund (ETF) this week. The Schwab Crypto Thematic ETF aims to provide investors with global exposure to companies that may benefit from the development or utilization of cryptocurrencies and other digital assets. This move positions Schwab to compete with major asset managers like Blackrock, Fidelity, and Vanguard in the crypto space.

title: From Profits to Pay, JPMorgan’s Gold Secrets Spill Out in Court
summary: The trial of JPMorgan Chase & Co.'s former head of precious metals, Michael Nowak, along with colleagues Gregg Smith and Jeffrey Ruffo, has revealed extensive details about the firm's precious metals trading desk, including its profitability and market share. The defendants are accused of manipulating gold and silver markets, and the jury has begun deliberations. The trial has highlighted how the business made over $100 million annually and the significant compensation received by the defendants.

title: Touchstone Strategic Income ETF
summary: This page provides a detailed profile of the Touchstone Strategic Income ETF (SIO), including its price, category, and recent performance. It outlines key vitals such as its inception date, expense ratio, asset under management (AUM), and a breakdown of its top holdings, primarily consisting of U.S. Treasury bonds and corporate debt. The profile also offers comparisons with other ETFs in its category regarding size, valuation, dividends, fund flows, and ESG scores.

title: Banamex, la filial mexicana de Citi, podría atraer ofertas de hasta US$8.000 millones
summary: Citigroup's Mexican unit, Banamex, is expected to attract bids between $7 billion and $8 billion as the number of potential buyers narrows. Key bidders include Grupo Financiero Banorte, Carlos Slim's Grupo Financiero Inbursa, mining magnate Germán Larrea, and Grupo Financiero Mifel. Banco Santander previously withdrew after its $6 billion offer was rejected.

title: VINCI Airports becomes the leading shareholder of the Mexican airport operator OMA
summary: VINCI Airports has become the leading shareholder of Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte (OMA) by acquiring a 29.99% stake. This acquisition adds 13 airports in Mexico, serving 23 million passengers in 2019, to VINCI's portfolio. The move further consolidates VINCI Airports' position as the world's leading private airport operator and expands its international presence.

title: Ron Kruszewski, Chairman and CEO of Stifel Financial Corp.
summary: This article provides a profile of Ron Kruszewski, the Chairman and CEO of Stifel Financial Corp. It details his extensive career at Stifel since 1997, his leadership roles in prominent financial industry associations like the American Securities Association and SIFMA, and his involvement in various community and philanthropic organizations. The piece also highlights his recognition with the Horatio Alger Award and his membership in The Wall Street Journal’s CEO Council.

title: TD buying Cowen for US$1.3B in U.S. investment banking push
summary: Toronto-Dominion Bank announced its agreement to acquire Cowen Inc. for US$1.3 billion, or US$39 per share, aiming to expand its U.S. investment banking presence. The deal, financed by selling shares in The Charles Schwab Corp., has drawn analyst warnings about talent retention and the competitiveness of TD's U.S. investment banking ambitions against Wall Street giants. This acquisition marks TD's second major U.S. takeover this year, following the announced purchase of First Horizon Corp.

title: Equifax Sent Banks Wrong Credit Scores for Consumers, WSJ Says (EFX)
summary: Equifax Inc. reportedly sent inaccurate credit scores for millions of U.S. consumers to banks and lenders between mid-March and early April. These errors affected applications for auto loans, mortgages, and credit cards at major institutions like JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, and Ally Financial. Equifax began disclosing these errors to lenders in May.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | Equifax Sent Lenders Inaccurate Credit Scores on Millions of Consumers
summary: Equifax provided inaccurate credit scores to millions of U.S. consumers seeking various loans for a three-week period earlier this year due to a technology coding issue. These erroneous scores, sometimes off by 20 points or more, may have led to altered interest rates or rejected loan applications for consumers. The company has since fixed the error and stated that only a small number of consumers may have received a different credit decision.

title: JPMorgan Chase Hires Charles Lim to Enhance 'Security, Efficiency and Robustness of Financial and Banking Services'
summary: JPMorgan Chase has hired Charles Lim, a leading expert in quantum communication and cryptography, as its global head of quantum communication and cryptography. Lim, formerly an assistant professor at the National University of Singapore, will focus on innovative digital solutions to enhance the security and efficiency of financial services. This move underscores JPMorgan Chase's commitment to exploring quantum technology's potential benefits and addressing potential threats in the financial industry.

title: Citigroup to launch hiring spree
summary: Citigroup announced plans to hire 500 employees over the next three years for its new "Wealth at Work" division, a move that bucks the recent trend of layoffs and hiring freezes across several industries. This initiative aims to serve junior employees at private equity and accounting firms, with the goal of retaining these clients as their careers advance. The article contrasts Citigroup's expansion with widespread workforce reductions and hiring slowdowns seen in tech, media, and other financial companies.

title: AES El Salvador obtiene crédito por 348 millones de dólares
summary: AES El Salvador, a subsidiary of the US-based AES Corporation, secured a $348 million syndicated credit from a group of national and international banks, led by Banca de Inversión Bancolombia and Banco Agrícola. A significant portion of these funds will be used to repurchase primary bonds previously issued by the company in international markets. This financial move aims to strengthen the company's capital structure and underlines its presence in the Salvadoran energy sector.

title: TD Bank Group to acquire U.S. investment firm Cowen Inc. for US$1.3 billion
summary: TD Bank Group announced its acquisition of U.S. investment firm Cowen Inc. for US$1.3 billion in cash, aiming to bolster its investment arm, TD Securities, and accelerate its international investment banking growth. The deal will expand TD Securities' capabilities in global equity sales, trading, and research coverage, with the combined business operating as TD Cowen. TD expects to spend US$200 million on retention costs and US$450 million for integration, with the transaction expected to close in Q1 2023.

title: TD to buy Cowen for US$1.3-billion, doubling down on ambitious U.S. expansion plans
summary: Toronto-Dominion Bank (TD-T) is set to acquire New York-based investment bank Cowen Inc. for US$1.3-billion, accelerating its U.S. capital markets expansion. This acquisition follows TD's US$13.4-billion bid for First Horizon Corp. and aims to strengthen TD's presence in U.S. equities, M&A advisory, and research, areas where it previously faced gaps. The deal is part of TD's aggressive U.S. strategy, coming after a significant investment in First Horizon and a recent executive team overhaul.

title: J.P. Morgan Builds Out Secondaries Capabilities with Senior Private Credit, Private Equity Hires
summary: J.P. Morgan Global Alternatives has expanded its secondaries capabilities by hiring Andrew Carter as Head of Private Credit Secondaries and Tim Henn as a lead Portfolio Manager for Secondaries within the Private Equity Group. These strategic appointments aim to address increasing client demand for liquidity and returns beyond traditional public markets. The firm emphasizes the critical role of private credit and private equity in future client portfolios.

title: White Mountains completes sale of NSM to Carlyle
summary: White Mountains Insurance Group has finalized the sale of its NSM Insurance Group to investment funds associated with Carlyle for $1.775 billion. This transaction is anticipated to generate a gain of approximately $280 to White Mountains' adjusted book value per share and significantly increase its undeployed capital. J.P. Morgan Securities LLC advised White Mountains and NSM, while Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC advised Carlyle.

title: J.P. Morgan hires trio of private bankers in Chicago
summary: J.P. Morgan Private Bank has hired a three-person team of private bankers from Citigroup in Chicago. This team previously managed over $2 billion in client assets. The move is part of J.P. Morgan's broader strategy to expand its wealth management operation, with plans to hire more advisors in the Chicago region and nationally.

title: Ôm tiền gửi tiết kiệm, hiệu suất từ đầu năm của Passion Investment vượt trội các quỹ đầu tư “full” cổ phiếu
summary: The article highlights that Passion Investment, by holding savings deposits, achieved a superior year-to-date performance compared to other "full" equity investment funds, especially amidst unfavorable market fluctuations. While many large investment funds experienced significant losses, Passion Investment managed to stay in the upper half of the rankings in July and emerged as the top-performing institution year-to-date, primarily due to its strategic focus on fixed-income assets. This strategy allowed it and other bond funds to maintain positive returns, contrasting sharply with the negative performances of most equity-heavy funds.

title: Lineage Logistics Closes Acquisition of VersaCold Logistics Services
summary: Lineage Logistics has completed its acquisition of VersaCold Logistics Services, a major cold chain service provider in Canada. This acquisition expands Lineage's Canadian operations and aims to offer more efficient cross-border solutions for customers in North America. The combined entity will leverage complementary facility networks, integrated transportation offerings, and shared expertise to enhance the global food supply chain.

title: Morgan Stanley Advisor Uses Sustainable Investing Expertise To Manage $2.5 Billion For Clients
summary: Katy Zhao, a Senior Vice President at Morgan Stanley Wealth Management, manages $2.5 billion in assets for clients, leveraging her expertise in sustainable investing. She developed Morgan Stanley's first ESG model portfolio and integrates ESG factors into her investment philosophy, an approach popular with her client base. Zhao focuses on direct investments rather than mutual funds or ETFs, positioning client portfolios defensively amidst a deleveraging cycle, and aims to help clients navigate market volatility and avoid social media-driven investment misconceptions.

title: Faulty Equifax Credit Score Reporting Prevents Consumers From Getting Auto Loans, Mortgages and Credit Cards
summary: Equifax erroneously reported faulty credit scores to millions of American consumers between mid-March and April, affecting applications for auto loans, mortgages, and credit cards. The errors, some as significant as 20 points, led to some consumers being rejected or receiving incorrect interest rates. Equifax attributed the issue to a coding error, stating it has been fixed, and that only a small number of consumers may have been negatively impacted.

title: Disney class action alleges Visa, Mastercard charge high transaction fees
summary: The Walt Disney Co. has filed a class action lawsuit against Visa and Mastercard, alleging that the payment companies colluded to force merchants to pay excessively high transaction fees for over a decade, violating antitrust laws. Disney claims these "interchange fees" are supracompetitive and seeks damages, fees, and costs, arguing that more competition between card-issuers would benefit both merchants and consumers. This action follows Disney's decision to opt out of a previous $6 billion multidistrict litigation settlement with Visa and Mastercard regarding similar fee-fixing allegations.

title: Most Influential Women: Emily Nachlas, Western Alliance Bancorporation
summary: Emily Nachlas, Chief Risk Officer at Western Alliance Bancorporation, has been recognized as one of Arizona's Most Influential Women of 2022 by Az Business and AZRE magazines. The article highlights her extensive experience, her role as a mentor, and her philanthropic efforts in fostering over 50 small dogs. Nachlas also cites Judy Sheindlin (Judge Judy) as a significant source of inspiration.

title: Una empresas argentina que desarrolla soluciones digitales de pagos recibió una inversión millonaria
summary: Geopagos, an Argentine company specializing in digital payment solutions, has secured a significant investment of US$35 million in its first institutional funding round. The funding, led by Riverwood Capital with participation from Endeavor Catalyst, will be used to develop new omnichannel payment products, enable new acceptance methods, and open its API platform. Geopagos serves major financial institutions and fintechs across 15 Latin American countries, processing over 150 million transactions and more than US$5 billion annually.

title: Wells Fargo could be expanding its North Texas footprint with a regional hub
summary: Wells Fargo is considering a significant expansion in North Texas, seeking $31 million in economic incentives from the Irving City Council for a new regional hub. The proposed development in Las Colinas would include an 800,000-square-foot office space for up to 4,000 employees, along with a parking garage and lake reclamation project. Project developer KDC, known for developing other large corporate campuses in North Texas, is involved in the plans.

title: 5 Minutes With ... Jamie Dimon, chairman and CEO of JPMorgan Chase & Co.
summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon was in Boston to announce plans for Chase Bank to significantly expand its footprint in Massachusetts, aiming to grow from 36 to nearly 90 branches by 2025. This expansion follows Dimon's previous visit to open a new branch in Mattapan and poses a potential long-term threat to current Boston banks.

title: Geopagos, fintech argentina de aceptación de pagos, levantó US$35 millones • Contxto
summary: Geopagos, an Argentine fintech specializing in payment acceptance solutions, has raised $35 million in its first institutional financing round led by Riverwood Capital. The company, founded in 2013, provides technology for businesses to launch or scale their payment processing operations in 15 Latin American countries. This investment will accelerate Geopagos's growth across the region and increase R&D efforts.

title: Jefferies Hires JPMorgan Chase’s Co-Head of North America M&A
summary: Jefferies Financial Group Inc. has hired Chris Roop, formerly the co-head of North America mergers and acquisitions at JPMorgan Chase & Co. Roop, a prominent health-care dealmaker based in Chicago, previously led JPMorgan's M&A health-care coverage and has also worked at Perrigo Co. The move signifies a significant addition to Jefferies' M&A team.

title: Use of credit cards, personal loans surges, but 'it's not a red flag,’ expert says
summary: The use of credit cards and personal loans reached record highs in the second quarter of 2022, driven by an increase in loans to subprime borrowers. TransUnion's Michele Raneri notes that while delinquencies are approaching pre-pandemic levels, a strong job market prevents this surge from being a "red flag." The primary indicator of a consumer's ability to repay is employment, which remains robust despite high inflation and rising interest rates.

title: Breaking: Class Action Lawsuits Filed Against Coinbase As It Reaches Supreme Court
summary: Three new class action lawsuits have been filed against Coinbase and its executives, accusing the company of making false and misleading statements, failing to disclose bankruptcy risks, and violating securities law. These lawsuits follow Coinbase's move to the Supreme Court to settle two previous class actions related to scam and Dogecoin sweepstakes. The new litigation alleges Coinbase failed to communicate regulatory scrutiny and that its shares dropped due to these issues, even as CEO Brian Armstrong apologized for late disclosure.

title: What's next for Wells Fargo in its Texas expansion?
summary: Wells Fargo is set to make a significant investment in Texas with a new regional campus in Irving, following the city council's approval of $31 million in incentives. The development will include two 400,000-square-foot buildings, potentially housing 4,000 workers, and will be part of a larger mixed-use project. This expansion highlights North Texas's growing prominence as a financial hub, attracting major firms like Charles Schwab, JPMorgan Chase, and Goldman Sachs.

title: Morgan Stanley job posting points to wide-ranging crypto plans
summary: Morgan Stanley Wealth Management is seeking a product development manager to focus on building new crypto products across various business lines, as indicated by a recent LinkedIn job posting. This move suggests the financial giant is intensifying its commitment to cryptocurrency offerings, looking to expand beyond the private passive fund it launched in March 2021. The new role aims to create packaged products and indexes, potentially collaborating with over 200 asset management firms to enhance product usage for financial advisors.

title: MEGL - Magic Empire Global Ltd Stock Price and Quote
summary: This article provides detailed financial information and recent news headlines for Magic Empire Global Ltd (MEGL), a Hong Kong-based company specializing in corporate finance advisory and underwriting services. It includes stock performance metrics, insider ownership data, and a timeline of news events related to its IPO, stock volatility, and Nasdaq compliance issues.

title: Ex-JPMorgan CEO says highly successful people get outside their comfort zones: 'That's how you keep growing'
summary: Former JPMorgan Chase CEO Bill Harrison emphasizes that highly successful individuals consistently step outside their comfort zones to foster continuous growth. Harrison, who led JPMorgan from 2000 to 2006, shared his personal experiences, including an initial reluctance to move to London for a management role that ultimately became a pivotal learning experience. His advice is supported by recent psychological research indicating that embracing discomfort can lead to greater learning and personal development.

title: Watkins Advises on Global Blood Therapeutics’ US$5.4 Billion Sale to Pfizer
summary: Latham & Watkins LLP advised J.P. Morgan Securities LLC and Centerview Partners LLC, financial advisors to Global Blood Therapeutics (GBT), on its US$5.4 billion sale to Pfizer Inc. The acquisition aims to enhance Pfizer's rare hematology offerings and reinforce its commitment to addressing critical needs in the underserved sickle cell disease community with GBT's pipeline.

title: Will Change in Control at HDFC AMC Impact Your Investments?
summary: HDFC Ltd. has received in-principle approval from SEBI for a change in control of HDFC AMC, shifting from HDFC Ltd. to HDFC Bank as part of their merger. This change is not expected to affect the day-to-day operations or investment processes of HDFC AMC, though it may indirectly impact schemes with high exposure to the merged entity due to regulatory caps on single-stock holdings. Investors are advised against immediate portfolio action unless fund performance is unsatisfactory over a longer duration or the scheme's objectives change.

title: Idaho Rep. Russ Fulcher joins House members’ letter opposing major banks’ abortion policies
summary: Idaho Rep. Russ Fulcher and 43 other U.S. House members sent a letter to the CEOs of eight major banks, including Bank of America and JPMorgan Chase, to express opposition to their policies covering employee travel expenses for abortions. The letter argues these policies are morally wrong and a violation of fiduciary responsibilities to shareholders, as they use investor resources for a social policy debate. Blaine Conzatti of the Idaho Family Policy Center also opposes such policies and is working on legislation to prohibit Idaho businesses from paying for abortion-related travel.

title: Groupon lays off hundreds of employees
summary: Groupon, the Chicago-based e-commerce marketplace, has laid off more than 500 employees, approximately 15% of its workforce, across various departments. This decision comes as the company restructures to focus on "self-service merchant acquisition capabilities," reduce cloud infrastructure, and rationalize its real estate footprint, citing that its overall business performance is not meeting anticipated levels and its cost structure is not aligned with its performance. Groupon joins a growing list of companies including Fender, Robinhood, Apple, Google, Vox Media, 7-Eleven, Meta, JPMorgan Chase & Co., Coinbase, Netflix, and Tesla that have recently announced layoffs or slowing hiring efforts ahead of an anticipated economic downturn.

title: Principal Financial’s benefits business jumps while AUM slumps in 2Q
summary: Principal Financial Group saw a strong performance in its employee benefits business in the second quarter, driven by growth in the small- and medium-sized business market, with premium and fees increasing by 11%. This growth partially offset a 9% decline in overall earnings to $423 million year-over-year, largely due to volatile markets, high inflation, and a slump in assets under management following the sale of its U.S. retail fixed annuity and universal life businesses. The company also returned $1.3 billion of capital to shareholders.

title: Bank price finishes higher
summary: The RG/BSX Index remained unchanged at 2,364.05, despite activity from Argus Group Holdings Ltd. The Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Limited saw a notable increase of 2.32% on the New York Stock Exchange. The article details these specific movements in the stock market.

title: John Morris
summary: John Morris was appointed Chief Financial Officer for Metra in July 2022, overseeing the Financial Affairs Department including Treasury, Accounting, and Budgets. He brings over 20 years of financial analysis experience from the credit card industry with companies like Synchrony, J.P. Morgan Chase, and HSBC, and previously worked at GE Capital, United Technologies, and the U.S. Army. Mr. Morris is a Certified Public Accountant, holding degrees from Northwestern University's Kellogg School of Management, University of Southern California's Viterbi School, and the United States Military Academy at West Point.

title: Staten Island’s Best Dressed: 2022 SIEDC Annual Awards Gala at Angelina’s Ristorante
summary: The 2022 SIEDC Annual Awards Gala, themed "Off to the Races," celebrated community and business leaders on Staten Island. Honorees included Diane Arneth, Carol Decina, Joseph Ferrara, Gina Laine, and Dr. Joanne Gerenser, with awards for "Best Dressed" attendees. The event, presented by Northfield Bank, featured entertainment, a silent auction, and horse racing games.

title: Has Inflation Peaked? Here's What the Experts Are Saying
summary: Inflation decelerated more than expected in July, leading to a split among economists and market strategists on whether this marks a peak in inflation and how it will impact Federal Reserve policy. While some see the report as positive evidence for a softer landing and less aggressive rate hikes, others emphasize the need for sustained slowdowns before the Fed becomes confident in controlling price pressures.

title: JPMorgan Chase Avoided Public Punishment From CFPB Under Trump After Discovery of Alleged Fake Accounts
summary: JPMorgan Chase (JPM) allegedly avoided public sanctions from the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) during the Trump administration for creating fake accounts, despite the agency identifying serious instances at four banks after the Wells Fargo scandal. The CFPB's enforcement unit investigated Chase for several years but closed the matter in early 2020. This incident highlights a broader trend during the Trump administration where financial institutions like TD Bank (TD) also faced private reprimands instead of public penalties for similar misconduct, drawing criticism from lawmakers like Senator Elizabeth Warren.

title: JGRO Stock Fund Price and Chart — AMEX:JGRO
summary: This article provides detailed information about the JPMorgan Active Growth ETF (JGRO), including its price, key statistics like AUM and expense ratio, and investment strategy. It covers the fund's asset allocation, top holdings, and answers frequently asked questions about ETFs and JGRO's performance. The article also includes technical analysis indicators for JGRO.

title: Benchmark Rate SOFR Has Caught On. But One Version Is Costing Companies More to Hedge
summary: Companies are facing higher hedging costs for a forward-looking interest-rate benchmark, Term SOFR, which is replacing the problematic Libor rate. While SOFR is gaining wide acceptance, its term version is more expensive to hedge than the overnight rate, adding to expenses for finance chiefs seeking to control costs. This difference is attributed to restrictions on banks, despite the benefit of Term SOFR in helping businesses forecast cash flows.

title: UBS’s Broker Count Has Slipped to Almost 5,600–Sources
summary: Headcount at UBS Wealth Management USA has fallen to just over 5,600, a significant decline from 2018 figures and below publicly reported numbers for its Americas unit. This reduction is partly strategic, as UBS focuses on more productive advisors, although the firm is also becoming more aggressive in recruiting veteran producers to boost net new fee-based assets. The overall trend of declining sales forces and an aging workforce is not unique to UBS, affecting other wirehouses as well.

title: PNC Drops Another Type of Fee After Overhauling Overdraft Policy
summary: PNC Financial Services Group Inc. has eliminated non-sufficient fund (NSF) fees, joining other large banks in removing charges that have drawn criticism from politicians and consumer advocates. These fees were previously charged when a transaction was returned due to insufficient funds in a customer's account. PNC had already removed NSF fees from its Virtual Wallet Spend feature and is now extending this policy to other personal checking-account options.

title: Data science major learns memorable lessons at JPMorgan internship
summary: Angel Lee, a junior information systems major at Virginia Commonwealth University, completed a six-week summer internship with JPMorgan Chase & Co. in Plano, Texas, through the Advancing Black Pathways Fellowship. The VCU Internship Funding Program provided her with crucial financial assistance for housing, enabling her participation. Lee found valuable insights into data analysis and the importance of authenticity in the workplace, and JPMorgan has invited her to apply for future internships.

title: BNY Mellon sets stage for next CEO Robin Vince - Pittsburgh Business Times
summary: BNY Mellon is preparing for the transition of its CEO role to Robin Vince, effective August 31, 2022. The Pittsburgh Business Times reported on this change in leadership for the financial institution. The article briefly previews the upcoming leadership change without delving into extensive details.

title: 10 Big Named Companies With Huge Free Cash Flows @Ycharts
summary: This article identifies ten large-cap companies that demonstrate significant free cash flow relative to their market capitalization, based on the price to free cash flow (P/FCF) ratio. The author explains that P/FCF is a robust valuation metric as it accounts for capital expenditures, providing a more accurate picture of cash available for non-asset-related growth. The list includes companies from various sectors like finance, energy, and technology, each with their respective market caps, free cash flows, and P/FCF ratios.

title: J.P. Morgan Asset Management Announces Liquidation of Two Exchange-Traded Funds
summary: J.P. Morgan Asset Management announced the upcoming liquidation and dissolution of two exchange-traded funds, JPMorgan U.S. Minimum Volatility ETF (JMIN) and JPMorgan U.S. Dividend ETF (JDIV). Shareholders can sell their holdings on NYSE Arca until September 6, 2022, with the liquidation date set for September 14, 2022. Those holding shares after this date will receive a cash distribution equal to the net asset value.

title: Bank of New York Mellon Corp. stock rises Friday, still underperforms market
summary: Shares of Bank of New York Mellon Corp. rallied 1.19% on Friday, but the stock still underperformed the broader market, which saw the S&P 500 Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average rise more significantly. Despite this gain, the stock remains considerably below its 52-week high. Its performance was mixed compared to competitors like JPMorgan Chase & Co., Citigroup Inc., and Wells Fargo & Co.

title: 3 ways treasury can make an impact on ESG goals
summary: Treasury teams are uniquely positioned to advance Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) goals within organizations by aligning their operations with overarching ESG strategies. The article outlines three key areas where treasury can make an impact: reducing carbon footprint through electronic processes, cultivating a diverse workforce by offering benefits like earned wage access and financial wellness programs, and promoting sustainable business operations through setting ESG standards for partners and automating processes. By taking these actions, treasury can lead by example, drive efficiency, and contribute significantly to a company's overall ESG performance.

title: Wells Fargo plans retreat from mortgage business
summary: Wells Fargo & Co. is planning to significantly reduce its mortgage business after years of regulatory scrutinized and changes in leadership. The bank, which once held a dominant share of the U.S. home loan market, aims to focus on lending to existing customers and scale back operations like correspondent mortgage lending and third-party servicing. This strategic shift reflects a broader industry trend among large banks to moderate their mortgage exposure following the 2008 financial crisis and ongoing regulatory challenges.

title: Saudi PIF buys shares in Alphabet, Zoom and Microsoft in U.S. shopping spree
summary: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) has significantly increased its U.S. stock holdings, acquiring shares in major tech companies like Alphabet, Zoom Video, and Microsoft. The sovereign wealth fund also invested in JPMorgan, BlackRock, Starbucks, and several other prominent companies. These investments are part of the PIF's strategy to diversify Saudi Arabia's economy away from oil and build an international investment portfolio.

title: John Deere tractors are getting the jailbreak treatment from hackers
summary: Hackers are now jailbreaking John Deere tractors, highlighting the broader "right-to-repair" issue beyond smartphones. A hacker, "Sick Codes," demonstrated at Def Con how to access and control John Deere tractors' onboard systems, revealing vulnerabilities and the importance for farmers to be able to repair their own software. This development underscores the need to balance farmers' access to essential machinery systems with industry-wide security to prevent agricultural disruptions.

title: Saudi PIF buys shares in Alphabet, Zoom and Microsoft in US shopping spree
summary: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) significantly expanded its US stock portfolio in the second quarter, investing approximately $40.8 billion. The fund acquired shares in major tech companies like Alphabet, Zoom Video, and Microsoft, alongside holdings in JPMorgan, BlackRock, Starbucks, Adobe, and others. The PIF, managing $620 billion in assets, is a key instrument in Saudi Arabia's strategy to diversify its economy away from oil.

title: Pomelo Launches Family Credit Cards to Combine Credit and International Money Transfer
summary: Pomelo is introducing a new family credit card system that allows primary accountholders to issue up to four cards to friends and family overseas, eliminating international money transfer fees by using credit rails. The company, launched with $70 million in Seed funding, aims to help users build credit in the U.S. while providing financial access to loved ones in emerging economies. The service is initially available for transfers between the U.S. and the Philippines, where users can manage spending limits and track card usage via an app.

title: Citigroup Inc. stock underperforms Tuesday when compared to competitors despite daily gains
summary: Shares of Citigroup Inc. (C) rose 0.20% on Tuesday to $54.18, despite a broadly positive trading session for the stock market. However, Citigroup underperformed compared to key competitors like JPMorgan Chase & Co., Bank of America Corp., and Wells Fargo & Co., which saw larger gains. The company's stock closed significantly below its 52-week high, and trading volume was below its 50-day average.

title: Things are getting tricky for State Street’s blockbuster acquisition
summary: State Street's $3.5 billion acquisition of Brown Brothers Harriman's investor services business is facing significant delays and increased federal scrutiny, nearly a year after its announcement. President Biden's administration has made bank mergers a target of closer examination, leading State Street to consider restructuring the deal, including a potential price adjustment, hoping to close by the end of 2022. The extended timeline and regulatory challenges have fueled uncertainty among shareholders, though State Street remains committed to the transaction.

title: JPMorgan Chase invests $1.5 million in initiative for women of color
summary: JPMorgan Chase has invested $1.5 million in an "equity design" institute in Columbus aimed at empowering women of color to develop solutions for systemic challenges like housing insecurity and childcare access. The initiative, a collaboration between Zora’s House, the Women’s Fund of Central Ohio, Columbus College of Art and Design (CCAD), and Fringe 22, will train women to apply design principles for more equitable systems. JPMorgan Chase's investment is part of its broader Racial Equity Commitment to bridge equity gaps and support communities of color.

title: FACTBOX U.S., European banks could lose over $5 bln from risky buyout loans
summary: Major U.S. and European banks are facing significant write-downs on leveraged and bridge loans due to rising interest rates and market turmoil. Bank of America, Citigroup, Wells Fargo, Credit Suisse, JPMorgan, Deutsche Bank, and Barclays have reported substantial losses, collectively exceeding $1 billion, in the second quarter of 2022. This comes as higher rates make it harder for banks to offload debt, leading to mark-to-market losses on these risky buyout loans.

title: Executive Leadership Drives JPMorgan Chase’s Delivery Of Customer And Business Value From Data Investments
summary: JPMorgan Chase, under executive leadership, is aggressively leveraging data and analytics to enhance customer experience and drive business value, as highlighted at its Investor Day. The bank's Chief Data & Analytics Officer, Mark Birkhead, details initiatives across retail banking and wealth management, focusing on real-time personalization, extended intelligence, and a massive data modernization effort, including cloud migration and a "data marketplace." This commitment to data is a long-term strategic priority, aiming for significant value generation from AI and machine learning investments while emphasizing data responsibility and ethical use through programs like the Data for Good Hackathon.

title: Anshu Jain, Who Took Deutsche Bank to Wall Street, Dies at 59 (Published 2022)
summary: Anshu Jain, the former co-chief executive of Deutsche Bank, died at 59 from intestinal cancer. He was instrumental in transforming Deutsche Bank from a conservative German lender into a Wall Street investment banking powerhouse. However, his aggressive pursuit of complex financial products ultimately led to his resignation due to regulatory problems and a downturn in the bank's fortunes.

title: Barclays: No retreat from Africa but a reset, says Amol Prabhu
summary: Amol Prabhu, Barclays Country CEO for South Africa and Market Head for Africa, clarifies that Barclays has not retreated from Africa but has repositioned its business model to focus on private, investment, and corporate banking. He explains the rationale behind divesting from ABSA and the retail sector, emphasizing the bank's commitment to Africa through its global network and focus on high-value services for clients with overseas needs. Prabhu also highlights the growing opportunities in African markets, particularly in wealth management and tech start-ups, and Barclays' strategy for growth and risk mitigation.

title: ATMD Group, who is behind a 32,000% IPO, is probed by Hong Kong regulator
summary: Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) is probing AMTD Group, the financial firm behind an IPO that surged over 32,000% in the US. The investigation into the company, led by Calvin Choi, predates the US listing of its unit AMTD Digital and focuses on its underwriting arrangements and alleged market manipulation practices involving small-cap IPOs. The probe adds to existing controversies surrounding Choi, including a two-year ban from the securities industry by the SFC and past accusations of financial fraud.

title: US, European banks could lose over $5bn from risky buyout loans
summary: Top US and European banks face potential losses of over $5 billion from leveraged and bridge loans due to rising interest rates and a slowdown in the leveraged buyout market. Banks like Bank of America are particularly exposed, having committed to financing large buyout deals, while difficulties in offloading debt to investors are forcing underwriters to sell at a discount. The market disruption is primarily attributed to the Federal Reserve's aggressive monetary policy tightening to combat inflation.

title: JP Morgan AM launches US small cap ETF
summary: J.P. Morgan Asset Management (JPMAM) has launched a new US small-cap equity ETF, the JPM BetaBuilders US Small Cap Equity UCITS ETF (BBSC), expanding its passive BetaBuilders range. The ETF tracks the Morningstar US Small Cap Target Market Exposure index, offering exposure to approximately 1,500 small-cap companies with a total expense ratio (TER) of 0.14%. This launch responds to ongoing demand for US equities and follows JPMAM's earlier expansion of its ETF offerings in 2022.

title: First Internet Bank launches small-business account
summary: First Internet Bank has launched a new checking account, "Do More Business Checking," specifically designed for small-business owners. This product allows business owners to earn interest, make unlimited transactions, and link various financial accounts for a comprehensive view of both business and personal finances. The initiative aims to simplify day-to-day operations for small businesses and tap into a significant market opportunity previously dominated by third-party providers and fintechs.

title: Clayton-based investment manager launches new fund designed to reach the 'masses'
summary: Argent Capital Management, an investment firm based in Clayton, has launched a new mid-cap exchange-traded fund (ETF). This fund is designed to make their investment strategy, previously exclusive to investors with $250,000, accessible to a broader range of smaller-scale investors.

title: Bank share price declines on NYSE
summary: The Royal Gazette/BSX Index increased by 1.59 percent to 2,401.75, primarily driven by insurance stocks. While Argus Group Holdings Ltd and BF&M Ltd saw their share prices rise, The Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Limited experienced a decline of 3.38 percent on the New York Stock Exchange.

title: Lead FedEx Ground contractor says he may shut his business by Nov. 25
summary: Spencer Patton, a prominent FedEx Ground contractor, has threatened to shut down his business by November 25 if FedEx Ground does not renegotiate contracts to address rising costs. Patton, who leads an effort to highlight financial struggles among contractors, is pushing for better financial support, especially for the upcoming holiday season. FedEx Ground, however, states that its model remains strong and that many contracts have recently been renegotiated.

title: Heartland Express acquires CFI assets for $525 million
summary: Heartland Express acquired Contract Freighters Inc.'s (CFI) truckload and Mexican logistics units from TFI International for $525 million, making it the eighth-largest truckload fleet in the U.S. The deal, funded by cash and debt, is expected to immediately boost Heartland's earnings and increase its annual revenue to approximately $1.3 billion. CFI will continue to operate under its existing brand and management team, with Heartland aiming for an 85% or better adjusted operating ratio within three years.

title: 5 Handy Online Payment Partners for Your Convenience
summary: This article highlights five convenient online payment partners in the Philippines: BancNet, DragonPay, PesoPay, WeePay, and PayEasy. These platforms cater to various payment methods, including bank accounts, over-the-counter transactions, credit cards, and e-wallets, making online commerce more accessible for both consumers and merchants. The aim is to simplify online transactions by offering diverse options for paying bills and purchasing goods.

title: Dive Deposits: BofA, RBC eye ‘balance’ in data- or emotion-based stances
summary: Bank of America and Royal Bank of Canada are approaching recent narratives with contrasting communication styles. While BofA uses data to highlight a 90% drop in overdraft-related revenue following policy changes, RBC appeals to emotion in its push for employees to return to the office more frequently, emphasizing human connection without concrete mandates. Despite their different methods, both banks mention the concept of "balance" in their statements regarding these distinct issues.

title: K-pop, Toyota’s platform for marketing in the US
summary: Toyota Motor Corp. leveraged KCON, a global K-pop festival, for its marketing efforts in the US, sponsoring the event for eight years. The KCON festival, organized by CJ ENM, saw a significant increase in attendance and a broadening demographic of K-pop fans, including more men and middle-aged enthusiasts. This partnership highlights the growing mainstream appeal of K-pop and its effectiveness as a platform for global brands to connect with consumers.

title: While mutual funds suffer losses, active ETFs continue to flourish
summary: Despite significant outflows and market declines impacting mutual funds, active Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) are experiencing strong growth. Investors worldwide withdrew a net US$640 billion from actively managed mutual funds in H1 2022, while active ETFs drew a net US$51.8 billion, demonstrating their increasing appeal, partly due to regulatory changes and structural advantages.

title: Goldman Sachs' long-running gender bias lawsuit set for June 2023 trial
summary: A U.S. federal judge has rejected Goldman Sachs' attempt to dismiss most of a 12-year-old class-action lawsuit alleging widespread gender bias in pay and promotions. The judge set a trial date for June 5, 2023, while narrowing the damages class to specific female vice presidents and associates. Goldman Sachs continues to deny wrongdoing and plans to vigorously defend itself against the claims.

title: Arista Stock Is a Cloud Winner. One Analyst Advises Caution.
summary: Arista Networks has demonstrated significant growth, with a 49% revenue increase in the June quarter, driven by strong demand for its networking hardware despite supply chain challenges. The company, a key provider to cloud computing and corporate data centers, has seen its stock perform better than competitors like Juniper Networks and Cisco Systems this year. However, one analyst advises caution regarding its future performance.

title: Goldman May Tap Brakes, Again, on Consumer Unit’s Next Big Thing
summary: Goldman Sachs is reportedly reconsidering the full-scale public launch of its online checking accounts for its consumer-banking arm, Marcus, due to persistent cost overruns and losses, which are projected to exceed $4 billion. Instead, the firm may opt for a more limited rollout to existing private-wealth clients and customers. This potential change reflects a shift in focus by leadership, including CEO David Solomon and deputy John Waldron, to manage investor expectations and prioritize wealth management over broader consumer banking initiatives, especially given the challenging regulatory environment and high customer acquisition costs in the industry.

title: MUFG’s Winter joins Lloyds Bank
summary: Lloyds Banking Group has appointed John Winter, former MUFG CEO for EMEA, as CEO of corporate and institutional banking, effective September 1st. Winter brings almost four decades of experience to the role and will lead the unit supporting corporate and financial institutions with turnover above £100 million. This appointment is part of a broader leadership restructuring effort at Lloyds Banking Group following a new internal structure implemented on July 1, 2022.

title: Morgan Stanley Advisor Uses Lessons From Growing Up In India To Manage $10 Billion For Clients
summary: Ron Basu, a Managing Director at Morgan Stanley Private Wealth Management, manages $10.4 billion in assets for clients, applying lessons learned from his upbringing in India, such as the importance of diversification due to currency depreciation and instability. Basu's investment philosophy emphasizes cashflow and compounding, and he prioritizes fundamental investing in tangible assets. He is currently navigating market volatility and geopolitical challenges by working with clients on hedging strategies and raising cash, while dealing with the stress of an interconnected global market.

title: JPMorgan Chase Applies to Open Its First Downtown Baltimore Branch
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. is set to open its first downtown Baltimore branch at 100 S. Charles St. in 2023, following an application filed with the federal Office of the Comptroller of the Currency. This move is part of the bank's aggressive expansion strategy in the region, aiming to open 70 new branches across Maryland, Washington, D.C., and Virginia by the end of 2025, doubling its initial goal. The new downtown branch will be Chase's seventh in Baltimore City and contributes to 13 total in Greater Baltimore.

title: The backlash against BlackRock, ESG investing intensifies
summary: Texas has barred 10 companies and 348 investment funds, including BlackRock and UBS, from doing business with the state because they "boycott energy companies" through their ESG investing strategies. This action follows a state law enacted last year and contributes to a growing trend among red states pushing back against "woke capitalism" and ESG funds. Despite the ban, companies like BlackRock assert their continued investment in the fossil fuel industry, and experts suggest the financial impact on Wall Street may be limited compared to actions by other large states.

title: BlackRock, BNP Paribas, UBS, Credit Suisse named to Texas ‘boycott’ list
summary: Texas has placed BlackRock, BNP Paribas, Credit Suisse, UBS, and six other financial firms on a list of companies that "boycott" the fossil-fuel sector, requiring state pension funds to divest from them. Texas Comptroller Glenn Hegar stated that the ESG movement has created an opaque system where some financial companies prioritize social agendas over shareholder interests. The listed companies have 90 days to demonstrate to the state that they do not boycott fossil fuels, while BlackRock has disputed the claim, highlighting its significant investments in Texas energy companies.

title: Japanese bank SMBC to launch US digital bank Jenius
summary: Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp. (SMBC) is set to launch Jenius Bank, a new digital consumer bank in the U.S., leveraging its subsidiary Manufacturers Bank. The initiative, backed by a $150 million investment, aims to tap into the North American retail market with initial offerings including personal loans, expanding to savings and checking accounts within the first year. Jenius Bank will prioritize a digital-first approach with a remote workforce and a commitment to customer service without punitive fees.

title: Investments based on strong ESG criteria shall increase by 2025
summary: Global investments based on Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) criteria are projected to exceed USD 50 billion by 2025, driven by increasing investor focus, regulatory changes, and a growing understanding that ESG integration does not sacrifice returns but can improve risk-return profiles. Despite macroeconomic uncertainties, the ESG investment boom is continuous, with companies demonstrating higher resilience and better risk management through strong ESG practices. Challenges remain in Latin America regarding corporate ESG reporting, senior management knowledge, and addressing the transition to a low-carbon economy.

title: Wind-Down of a Global Broker’s Equity Business
summary: FTI Consulting advised a top-tier global broker in the orderly wind-down of its equity business, which included structured equity finance, inter-dealer equity brokerage, and equity clearing services. The decision was prompted by a mismatch with the company's risk appetite and increased funding requirements. FTI Consulting helped plan, implement, and monitor the wind-down, ensuring all positions were closed and regulators were satisfied, with the process completed ahead of schedule.

title: FIS to Modernize Real-Time Payments Infrastructure and Central Bank Digital Currencies for Countries Around the World
summary: FIS has launched RealNet™ Central, a new central infrastructure payment solution designed to help central banks modernize or build real-time payment networks globally. Additionally, FIS is introducing a Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDC) Virtual Lab in collaboration with M10 Networks, enabling countries to experiment with and accelerate CBDC implementations. These initiatives aim to transform nations into digital, real-time inclusive economies and advance how the world pays.

title: NJ India, SBI and HDFC are top three distributors in terms of gross commission
summary: NJ India, SBI, and HDFC were the top three mutual fund distributors by gross commission in FY 2022, with NJ India receiving Rs. 1300 crore. SBI led in average AUM, reaching Rs. 1.20 lakh crore, followed by NJ India and HDFC Bank. The data highlights significant commission contributions from associated fund houses for several banks, such as SBI, HDFC, Axis, and ICICI.

title: What is quantitative easing and how does it impact markets?
summary: Quantitative easing (QE) is a monetary policy where central banks purchase assets to increase money supply and stimulate economic growth, typically used when interest rates are low and growth is stagnant. While it can stabilize economies and lower longer-term interest rates, QE carries risks such as inflation, asset bubbles, and income inequality. Its impact on financial markets includes boosting stock performance by lowering interest rates and making risk-on assets more appealing, and affecting exchange rates by devaluing the currency, which makes exports cheaper but imports more expensive.

title: Emaar jumps on recommendation to ditch foreign ownership cap
summary: Emaar Properties PJSC's shares rallied after its board recommended removing the 49 percent cap on foreign ownership. Shareholders will vote on the proposal on September 21. Major global investment firms like JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, and BlackRock are among its foreign owners.

title: Citi begins winding down operations in Russia
summary: Citigroup Inc. is officially beginning the wind-down of its consumer and local commercial banking operations in Russia after failing to find a buyer. This move comes after an initial announcement in April 2021 and an expansion of plans in March 2022 following Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Citi expects the wind-down process to take approximately 18 months.

title: New bank branch planned for downtown Baltimore
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co., the largest retail bank in the U.S., plans to open a new branch in downtown Baltimore at 100 S. Charles St., a location previously occupied by Bank of America. This move marks Chase's first downtown Baltimore branch, pending federal approval, and is part of its ongoing aggressive expansion in the region. The bank filed an application with the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency on August 12.

title: NJ home prices too high? Change laws to build more now, bankers say
summary: New Jersey bankers are advocating for changes to state laws to facilitate the construction of more housing units, arguing that the scarcity of homes is the primary driver of high prices. Christopher Maher of OceanFirst Bank and Michael Affuso of the New Jersey Bankers Association state that current inventory is insufficient, despite rising mortgage rates, and that local regulations restrict necessary development. They emphasize that increasing housing supply for all income levels, especially middle-class households, is crucial to address the cascading effect of inflated housing costs.

title: Clearance Holders Flagged by Feds for Gaming Credit Card Rewards
summary: This article discusses how individuals game credit card rewards programs by purchasing gift cards, converting them to money orders, and paying off credit card balances, generating significant tax-free income. It highlights the risks for security clearance holders who engage in this activity, as banks may file Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) due to large cash infusions. While not illegal, these SARs can lead to scrutiny during security clearance background investigations, potentially causing denials or revocations despite the activity's legality.

title: Meet the Most Trusted Financial Companies for 2022, according to MarketWatch and IBD survey
summary: A MarketWatch and Investor’s Business Daily survey identified the most trusted financial companies for 2022 amidst market volatility and economic uncertainty. USAA and Vanguard secured the top overall spots. Divisions of JPMorgan Chase, Primerica, and AllianceBernstein also made their debut on the ranking, which highlighted companies excelling in trustworthiness across various financial sectors.

title: Workspace Property Trust Buys Suburban Office Portfolio from Griffin Realty Trust for $1.1B
summary: Workspace Property Trust, leading a consortium of investors, has acquired a controlling interest in a national portfolio of suburban office buildings from Griffin Realty Trust for approximately $1.1 billion. The portfolio includes 41 properties across eight states, totaling 8 million square feet, with many being single-tenant, net-leased assets. This acquisition highlights a growing trend favoring suburban office properties, driven by demographic shifts and the perceived benefits of suburban locations over urban centers.

title: In the face of inflation, URBN embraces a diversified audience strategy
summary: URBN, the parent company of Urban Outfitters, Anthropologie, and other retailers, is adapting its strategy to inflation by catering to a bifurcated customer base. While its higher-priced brands like Anthropologie and Free People are flourishing, Urban Outfitters is struggling, leading the company to pursue aggressive promotions for the latter while investing in inventory for the former. URBN anticipates continued customer bifurcation and increased discounting across the apparel industry due to excess inventory.

title: MetLife Investment Management to acquire ESG fixed-income manager Affirmative Investment Management
summary: MetLife Investment Management is set to acquire Affirmative Investment Management, an ESG-focused fixed-income manager. The acquisition strengthens MetLife's offerings in the growing ESG investment space. This move will allow MetLife to expand its capabilities in responsible and sustainable investing.

title: Atlantic Union Bank Names Sherry Williams Chief Risk Officer
summary: Atlantic Union Bank has appointed Sherry Williams as its new Chief Risk Officer, effective by October 2022. Williams will oversee the company's enterprise and regulatory risk management functions. She brings 26 years of experience from previous roles at Amalgamated Bank, PwC, SunTrust Bank, State of Georgia, and Ernst & Young LLP, holding a doctorate in business administration and several professional certifications.

title: ESG investing a ‘dangerous placebo,’ former BlackRock head of sustainability says
summary: Tariq Fancy, former BlackRock head of sustainability, criticizes ESG investing as a "dangerous placebo," arguing that it is primarily marketing and does little to address environmental and social issues. He contends that ESG investing can even delay necessary government regulation, comparing it to giving "wheatgrass juice to a cancer patient" that delays "chemo." Fancy emphasizes that while climate risk is real and important for fiduciaries to manage, protecting portfolios from climate change is not the same as stopping climate change itself.

title: Card companies urged to code gun sellers
summary: Public officials and pension funds are increasing pressure on Visa, Mastercard, and American Express to create a unique merchant category code (MCC) for gun sellers. Proponents argue this code would help financial institutions track suspicious gun purchases, citing past incidents where firearms used in mass shootings were bought with credit cards. The International Standards Organization (ISO), which sets MCC standards, is considering the matter, while card companies remain largely uncommitted to publicly supporting the initiative.

title: Bed Bath & Beyond Inc. Announces Strategic Changes to Strengthen its Financial Positioning, Drive Growth and Better Serve Customers
summary: Bed Bath & Beyond Inc. announced strategic changes to strengthen its financial position, drive growth, and better serve customers, including securing over $500 million in new financing and implementing significant SG&A reductions. The company plans to refocus on national brands, optimize its store fleet by closing 150 lower-producing stores, and reduce its capital spending. Additionally, there are executive leadership changes and an interim financial update projecting a comparable sales decline of approximately 26% for Q2 fiscal 2022.

title: CAZ commits $1bn to Dyal Capital
summary: CAZ Investments has committed $1 billion to Dyal Capital Partners V, a GP stakes fund, bringing its total investment in GP stakes to $3 billion. Christopher Zook, chairman and CIO at CAZ, highlighted GP stakes as an appropriate cornerstone allocation due to its rare combination of downside protection, upside optionality, and attractive cash flow. Dyal, a division of Blue Owl, reportedly aimed to raise $9 billion for this fund, having previously raised the same amount for its prior fund.

title: CBOE's Weekly Market Recap: August 15 To August 19
summary: The CBOE's weekly market recap for August 15-19 indicates a potential end to the recent market rally, with experts from BlackRock and JPMorgan warning of resistance due to worsening global economic conditions. Major ETFs like SPY and several European ETFs, along with cryptocurrencies Bitcoin and Ethereum, experienced declines. Zoom Video Communications also saw its stock tumble after a revenue miss despite positive EPS.

title: Fiserv buys LR2 Group
summary: Global payments processor Fiserv has acquired independent sales organization The LR2 Group, which operates as The City POS, for $26 million. The acquisition, which was announced in Fiserv's 10-Q filing, enhances Fiserv's merchant services business and includes the retention of all 11 LR2 employees. This purchase is part of Fiserv's recent strategy of numerous, smaller acquisitions, following larger integration challenges from its 2019 acquisition of First Data.

title: Branch-closure freefall slows down: S&P Global
summary: U.S. banks are showing a slowdown in branch closures, with net closures significantly decreasing in Q2 2022 compared to the previous quarter. This trend suggests banks are seeking a balance between physical locations and digital channels, even as they continue to right-size their networks. Affluent, younger customers are still visiting branches more often than the average, indicating a persistent need for physical presence despite digital advancements.

title: Global PayEX optimises working capital via AR/AP automation
summary: Global PayEX offers a SaaS platform leveraging AI and ML to automate accounts receivable (AR) and accounts payable (AP) processes for B2B businesses. The platform, used by major corporates like 3M and Bridgestone, aims to streamline payments, reduce days sales outstanding (DSO), and enhance operational efficiencies. The company is also integrating embedded finance solutions by partnering with banks and lenders to provide credit lines within its digital ecosystem, expanding its reach globally from India to the US and Europe.

title: Citigroup's Russia exit removes one obstacle for CEO, but challenges remain
summary: Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser's decision to exit Russia and divest consumer businesses in 13 other countries is a step towards paring down risky assets and focusing on core operations. While analysts and investors view her strategy favorably, Fraser still faces significant challenges, including overhauling risk management systems mandated by U.S. regulators and a potentially deteriorating economic environment. The bank's stock remains undervalued compared to its peers, indicating a long road ahead for the turnaround effort.

title: Don't work in "lonely home silos", Jefferies CEO tells staff
summary: Jefferies Financial Group CEO Richard Handler has urged staff to return to the office consistently, stating that working together rather than in "lonely home silos" will help maximize the company's performance in the final quarter. While acknowledging a hybrid work format can be used when necessary, Handler emphasized the benefits of in-person collaboration. This move aligns with other major financial firms like Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and JPMorgan, which have also encouraged or mandated returns to office after pandemic-related disruptions.

title: Citigroup's Russia exit removes one obstacle for CEO, but challenges remain
summary: Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser is working to simplify the bank's structure and focus on core businesses by exiting Russia and paring down consumer operations in other countries. While investors and analysts acknowledge the positive direction, Fraser faces significant challenges, including overhauling risk management systems mandated by U.S. regulators and a potentially deteriorating economic environment. Despite these hurdles, some investors are showing patience with her long-term strategy for a "simpler, sounder bank."

title: TD Ameritrade: Roxanna Islam Talks Generating Income with CEFs
summary: Roxanna Islam of VettaFi discussed closed-end funds (CEFs) on TD Ameritrade Network, highlighting their appeal for income generation despite investor concerns about rising rates due to leverage. She noted that while prices and asset values fell during previous rate hikes, distribution cuts were less severe than expected and that CEFs like Invesco Senior Income Trust CEF VVR and PIMCO Dynamic Income Opportunities Fund PDO offer strong income potential and are less sensitive to rising rates.

title: Dow Inc. and LyondellBasell Stock Won’t Outperform Soon, Says J.P. Morgan
summary: J.P. Morgan analyst Jeffrey Zekauskas advised against investing new money in Dow Inc. and LyondellBasell Industries, stating that they are unlikely to outperform soon. Both companies received multiple downgrades this week.

title: UBS, Wealthfront Call Off Merger
summary: UBS Group AG and robo-advisor Wealthfront Inc. have terminated their planned $1.4 billion merger, with UBS instead providing nearly $70 million in financing for Wealthfront at the same valuation. Wealthfront's CEO expressed excitement about the company's future as an independent entity, while UBS reaffirmed its commitment to growth in the U.S. and its digital wealth management offerings. This decision comes after UBS's Q2 earnings fell short of expectations and as competitors push further into the self-directed market.

title: Catching peak bond yields
summary: This article discusses the current state of bond markets, particularly highlighting the risks of spread widening due to growth risk, central bank policies, and high debt levels. It suggests that locking in yields now is preferable to waiting for peak spreads, especially given the likelihood of continued volatility and potential for further deterioration in credit quality for high-yield issuers. The author recommends selective positioning in more defensive sectors and focusing on higher-rated investment-grade bonds.

title: ICICI Bank to raise 10,000 crore to maintain CRR and SLR
summary: ICICI Bank plans to raise up to Rs 10,000 crore through infrastructure bonds to fund project financing and affordable housing. These long-term bonds offer the advantage of exemption from statutory liquidity requirements (SLR) and cash reserve ratios (CRR), helping to mitigate asset-liability management issues. This move aligns with increased government capital spending and a significant rise in bank lending to the infrastructure sector in India.

title: Citigroup to Offer New Government-Sponsored Programs for Borrowers With Credit Challenges
summary: Citigroup announced the launch of two government-sponsored pilot programs under Project REACh to expand credit access for underserved communities. These programs, starting next year, will offer credit cards to individuals without traditional credit scores and make it easier for minority, women, and veteran-owned small businesses to obtain credit. This initiative aims to lower barriers to financial services, following similar efforts by other banks like JPMorgan Chase and Wells Fargo, and comes alongside Bank of America's zero down payment mortgage program for select communities.

title: AIG carve-out Corebridge Financial sets terms for $1.8 billion IPO, poised to be the largest IPO of 2022
summary: Corebridge Financial, an AIG carve-out focusing on retirement services and life insurance, has set terms for its initial public offering, aiming to raise $1.8 billion. This IPO, if successful, would be the largest of 2022, surpassing TPG's $1 billion offering. The company plans to offer 80 million shares at $21 to $24 each, implying a fully diluted market value of $14.7 billion, and intends to pay quarterly cash dividends.

title: How Ashton Woods grew their rebate revenue with One Card
summary: Ashton Woods, a luxury homebuilding company, partnered with J.P. Morgan to leverage its One Card commercial card solution to address payment challenges exacerbated by the pandemic. By migrating traditional payments to One Card, Ashton Woods facilitated online transactions, reduced processing times for permits, and navigated supply chain issues by paying suppliers digitally. This collaboration led to significant growth in business spending and rebate revenue, enhancing operational efficiency and positioning the company for continued success in a digital payments environment.

title: How does ETF redemption work, and what are economic impacts? – The FinReg Blog
summary: This article explores the mechanics and economic impacts of corporate bond ETF redemptions, particularly addressing discrepancies between ETF share prices and NAVs observed during crises like COVID-19. It investigates the incentives of ETFs and authorized participants (APs) in negotiating redemption baskets and analyzes the consequences for investors and market demand. The research finds that ETFs dispose of high price pressure bonds while APs select components that negatively co-move with the liquidity of their portfolios, reconciling debates between policymakers and practitioners.

title: AIG launches IPO capital raise for Corebridge
summary: American International Group (AIG) has initiated the initial public offering (IPO) for its majority-owned subsidiary, Corebridge Financial. AIG is offering 80 million shares of common stock at an anticipated price of $21 to $24 per share, with all net proceeds going directly to AIG. The shares are expected to trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker "CRBG."

title: Why Does VTS Need Another $125 Million?
summary: PropTech unicorn VTS recently secured $125 million in funding, led by CBRE, raising questions about its necessity given previous large funding rounds. The company aims to expand geographically and into new property types, necessitating acquisitions to broaden its offerings beyond Class A office leasing. This expansion, particularly into property management, pits VTS against some of its clients, notably JLL, and potentially gives CBRE influence to steer VTS against competitors, while also fortifying VTS against a potential tech market downturn.

title: FreshBooks taps PwC alum as new CFO
summary: FreshBooks, a cloud accounting software company, has appointed Wayne Jackson as its new CFO, effective September 6, 2022. Jackson, formerly CFO at Cantaloupe, Inc. and SecureWorks, brings extensive experience in M&A, international expansion, and financial management. His appointment comes as FreshBooks experiences growth, supported by a $125 million loan to fund strategic acquisitions and global expansion.

title: Episode #441: Marlena Lee, DFA – Value, Fama & Weathering Bear Markets
summary: This article features an interview with Marlena Lee, Global Head of Investment Solutions for Dimensional Fund Advisors (DFA), where she discusses her experience as a teaching assistant for Nobel laureate Eugene Fama and her insights on value investing. She also shares DFA's approach to weathering bear markets, applying factors to fixed income, and their recent entry into the ETF space. The discussion highlights the importance of diversification, long-term investing, and the role of financial advisors in managing investment emotions.

title: 5 Ways You Can Get Income From Your Investments Right Now |…
summary: This article outlines five easy ways investors can generate income from their investments, offering yields of up to 9%. It covers dividend-paying stocks and ETFs, bonds, REITs, Master Limited Partnerships (MLPs), and preferred shares. The author emphasizes the importance of diversifying an income portfolio to suit individual risk tolerance.

title: As merger deadline passes, State Street, Brown Brothers Harriman keep talking
summary: State Street Corp. and Brown Brothers Harriman are continuing talks regarding State Street's proposed acquisition of BBH's investor services division, despite missing their Sept. 6 merger deadline. The $3.5 billion deal has faced delays and scrutiny from federal regulators, leading to discussions about modified structures and financial terms. Both companies remain committed to the strategic rationale of the merger, though analysts suggest a price renegotiation might be necessary to reflect the timeline and any required changes for regulatory approval.

title: The US is a core market for UBS and its Financial Advisors | UBS United States of America
summary: This article highlights why UBS considers the US a core market for its wealth management business and financial advisors. It addresses common misconceptions about UBS's US operations, emphasizing its global scale, client-centric approach, and focus on supporting financial advisors with extensive resources and direct access to senior leadership. The piece also underlines UBS's leading position in wealth management and its commitment to continued investment in the US market, citing its high productivity per advisor and comprehensive service offerings.

title: Emerge to Launch 10 Sustainable ETFs That Are All Run by Women
summary: Emerge is launching 10 new sustainable ETFs, with each fund managed by women. These funds, listed on both the Cboe BZX Exchange in the US and the NEO Exchange in Canada, will invest in equity securities while excluding categories like gambling and chemical weapons. Emerge, Canada's first women-owned investment fund firm, also plans to debut a program called EMPWR to encourage more women to become investment managers for sustainability-focused funds.

title: Citigroup hires three for China securities business - source
summary: Citigroup has hired three bankers for its planned China securities business: Kenneth Koo as CEO, Rochelle Wei to lead its futures unit, and John Lu to head the onshore equities business. This move follows Citigroup's application for a mainland Chinese securities license last year, reflecting its efforts to expand its presence in the Chinese market.

title: JPMorgan Chase Invests in J2 Ventures
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. has made a strategic investment in J2 Ventures, a venture capital firm founded by U.S. Army veteran Alexander Harstrick and Jonathan Bronson, Ph.D. This investment is part of JPMorgan's Project Spark Initiative, which aims to provide capital to venture funds managed by emerging alternative managers with military service. J2 Ventures focuses on deep technology companies with applications in both government and private sectors, managing approximately $100 million in capital and including investments in companies like Oura Ring and Tasso Inc.

title: JPMorgan Chase Commercial Banking Appoints Eric Cohen to Lead Green Economy Team
summary: JPMorgan Chase Commercial Banking has appointed Eric Cohen as Head of Green Economy to lead its strategy for serving companies advancing decarbonization. Cohen, who previously worked at Fifth Third Bank, will focus on leveraging the bank's offerings to support green businesses. This appointment underscores JPMorgan's commitment to sustainable finance, having already mobilized $285 billion towards climate action and sustainable development.

title: Meet Wall St. thought leaders at Hankyung conference in NYC
summary: The Korea Economic Daily (KED) is hosting the "HANKYUNG Global Market Conference NYC 2022" in October, bringing together top Wall Street portfolio managers, analysts, and South Korean investors. The conference will feature prominent figures like Howard Marks and Eric S. Rosengren, covering investment strategies, macroeconomic risks, and emerging asset classes such as blockchain and NFTs. It also includes exclusive networking opportunities, a guided art tour at Christie's, and a visit to "Billionaires Row."

title: Deutsche Bank’s Chadha Sees 25% US Stock Slump if Recession Hits
summary: Deutsche Bank strategists, led by Binky Chadha, predict a potential 25% decline in US stocks if the economy enters a recession. They cite declining company profits, high stock valuations, and looming recession risks as major challenges for the equity market. Despite these risks, investor positioning in equities is currently low.

title: Longtime Adams Funds CEO Mark Stoeckle to retire; successor named
summary: Mark E. Stoeckle is retiring as CEO of Adams Funds, with James P. Haynie slated to take over. Stoeckle successfully guided Adams Funds through significant market volatility, including the Covid-19 pandemic.

title: SK Closes Sale of NuCera Solutions to Chase
summary: An affiliate of funds advised by SK Capital Partners has completed the sale of NuCera Solutions to Chase Corp. for $250 million. NuCera, a leading producer of specialty polymers, will be integrated into Chase's Adhesives, Sealants and Additives reporting unit.
